units.title: The instant something happens
units.summary: Literary ways to say 'the moment X happened, Y followed', plus expressions for starting and ending points like {を皮切[かわき]りに} and {を限[かぎ]りに}.

points.title: 〜が早[はや]いか
points.meaning: no sooner had X than Y; the instant X
points.structure: Verb (dictionary / た-form) + が早[はや]いか
points.explanation:
{〜が早[はや]いか} describes two actual events that happen almost on top of each other: the instant X happens, Y follows. Literally it is something like 'is X earlier, or (is Y)?' — they are so close you can hardly tell which came first.

The second clause describes something that actually happened (usually past tense), often a quick or impulsive reaction. You cannot use it for plans, requests or commands about the future.

**Register:** written and literary. You will see it in novels, essays and the occasional news story, and of course on the JLPT. In conversation people simply say {〜たとたん(に)} or {〜とすぐに}.

examples.jp: ベルが鳴[な]るが早[はや]いか、生徒[せいと]たちは教室[きょうしつ]を飛[と]び出[だ]した。
examples.en: The instant the bell rang, the students rushed out of the classroom.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は家[いえ]に帰[かえ]るが早[はや]いか、パソコンの電源[でんげん]を入[い]れた。
examples.en: No sooner had he got home than he switched on his computer.

examples.jp: 新製品[しんせいひん]は発売[はつばい]されるが早[はや]いか、ネット上[じょう]で完売[かんばい]となった。
examples.en: The new product sold out online the moment it was released.

examples.jp: 男[おとこ]は警官[けいかん]の姿[すがた]を見[み]るが早[はや]いか、人混[ひとご]みの中[なか]へ逃[に]げ込[こ]んだ。
examples.en: The moment the man caught sight of the police officer, he fled into the crowd.

points.notes: Not for the future or for your own intentions: {✕家[いえ]に着[つ]くが早[はや]いか電話[でんわ]してください} is wrong — use {着[つ]いたらすぐ} or {着[つ]き次第[しだい]}. Compare {や否[いな]や} and {なり} in this unit; all three mean 'as soon as', but {なり} stresses an unexpected action by the same person.

quiz.q: 子[こ]どもたちはおやつを見[み]る＿＿、テーブルに駆[か]け寄[よ]った。
quiz.en: The moment the children saw the snacks, they ran to the table.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は席[せき]に着[つ]く＿＿、ビールを注文[ちゅうもん]した。
quiz.en: No sooner had he sat down than he ordered a beer.

points.title: 〜や否[いな]や
points.meaning: as soon as; the moment (that)
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + や否[いな]や / + や
points.explanation:
{〜や否[いな]や} means 'the moment X happened, Y happened'. {否[いな]} means 'no', so the phrase is a frozen literary way of saying 'whether X or not' — i.e. before you could even say X had finished, Y occurred. A shortened form, just {〜や}, is also common in writing.

Like {が早[はや]いか}, it describes real past events, and the second clause is often a sudden reaction or a big change (prices crash, criticism floods in, applause erupts).

**Register:** formal written Japanese. It is a favourite in news reports and novels; you will rarely hear it in casual speech.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は電話[でんわ]を切[き]るや否[いな]や、泣[な]き出[だ]した。
examples.en: The moment she hung up, she burst into tears.

examples.jp: 幕[まく]が上[あ]がるや否[いな]や、会場[かいじょう]は大[おお]きな拍手[はくしゅ]に包[つつ]まれた。
examples.en: As soon as the curtain rose, the hall filled with loud applause.

examples.jp: 首相[しゅしょう]の発言[はつげん]が報[ほう]じられるや否[いな]や、批判[ひはん]が殺到[さっとう]した。
examples.en: The moment the prime minister's remarks were reported, a flood of criticism poured in.

examples.jp: 新[あら]たな規制[きせい]が発表[はっぴょう]されるや、株価[かぶか]は急落[きゅうらく]した。
examples.en: As soon as the new regulations were announced, share prices plunged.

points.notes: Don't confuse it with {〜か否[いな]か} ('whether or not'), as in {参加[さんか]するか否[いな]かを決[き]める} 'decide whether or not to take part'.

quiz.q: 試合[しあい]終了[しゅうりょう]の笛[ふえ]が鳴[な]る＿＿、選手[せんしゅ]たちはグラウンドに倒[たお]れ込[こ]んだ。
quiz.en: The moment the final whistle blew, the players collapsed onto the field.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は私[わたし]の顔[かお]を見[み]る＿＿否[いな]や、走[はし]り去[さ]った。
quiz.en: The moment he saw my face, he ran off.

points.title: 〜なり (as soon as)
points.meaning: as soon as (and then, unexpectedly)
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + なり
points.explanation:
{〜なり} says that as soon as someone did X, that same person immediately did Y — and Y is usually something surprising or out of the ordinary. Both actions belong to the same subject, and the sentence describes a past event.

Because it describes someone else's behaviour from the outside, it is mostly used about third persons, not about yourself.

**Register:** a bit literary, but it appears in novels, essays and storytelling, and older speakers may use it when telling an anecdote. Of the 'as soon as' expressions in this unit, it is the one you are most likely to meet in fiction.

examples.jp: 息子[むすこ]は帰[かえ]ってくるなり、「お腹[なか]すいた」と言[い]った。
examples.en: The moment my son got home, he said, 'I'm hungry.'

examples.jp: 父[ちち]は部屋[へや]に入[はい]ってくるなり、大声[おおごえ]で怒鳴[どな]った。
examples.en: As soon as my father came into the room, he started yelling.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]はそのメールを読[よ]むなり、顔色[かおいろ]を変[か]えた。
examples.en: The moment she read the email, her face changed colour.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]は報告書[ほうこくしょ]に目[め]を通[とお]すなり、担当者[たんとうしゃ]を呼[よ]びつけた。
examples.en: The president had barely glanced at the report before he summoned the person in charge.

points.notes: {なり} has several other uses — don't mix them up: {〜なり〜なり} 'either X or Y' ({電話[でんわ]なりメールなりで連絡[れんらく]して}), {〜たなり} 'and stayed that way' ({出[で]かけたなり戻[もど]らない}), and {〜なりに} 'in one's own way' (Unit 12).

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は椅子[いす]に座[すわ]る＿＿、眠[ねむ]り込[こ]んでしまった。
quiz.en: The moment he sat down in the chair, he fell fast asleep.

quiz.q: 姉[あね]は私[わたし]の顔[かお]を＿＿なり、笑[わら]い出[だ]した。
quiz.en: As soon as my sister saw my face, she burst out laughing.

points.title: 〜そばから
points.meaning: no sooner ... than (it's undone again); as fast as
points.structure: Verb (dictionary / た-form) + そばから
points.explanation:
{そば} means 'side, right next to'. {〜そばから} describes a frustrating cycle: as soon as you do something, it is immediately undone or followed by the same thing again — and this keeps repeating. You tidy up, and the kids mess it up again; you learn a word, and you've already forgotten it.

The key ideas are **repetition** and **futility**. It is not used for one single event.

**Register:** written or fairly formal, but it does show up in essays and in slightly wry everyday comments. It is less rare in speech than {が早[はや]いか}.

examples.jp: 片付[かたづ]けるそばから、子[こ]どもたちがおもちゃを散[ち]らかす。
examples.en: As fast as I tidy up, the kids scatter their toys again.

examples.jp: 新[あたら]しい単語[たんご]は覚[おぼ]えるそばから忘[わす]れてしまう。
examples.en: I forget new words as soon as I learn them.

examples.jp: 雪[ゆき]をかいたそばから、また積[つ]もっていく。
examples.en: No sooner have I shovelled the snow than it piles up again.

examples.jp: 給料[きゅうりょう]が入[はい]るそばから、ローンの返済[へんさい]に消[き]えていく。
examples.en: My salary vanishes into loan repayments as soon as it comes in.

points.notes: Compare {〜たとたん}: that is a single event ('the moment X, Y happened once'); {そばから} is a repeated, annoying pattern.

quiz.q: 部屋[へや]を掃除[そうじ]する＿＿、猫[ねこ]が毛[け]を散[ち]らかす。
quiz.en: As fast as I clean the room, the cat sheds fur everywhere again.

quiz.q: 説明[せつめい]を聞[き]いた＿＿忘[わす]れてしまうので、メモを取[と]るようにしている。
quiz.en: I forget explanations as soon as I hear them, so I make a point of taking notes.

points.title: 〜てからというもの
points.meaning: ever since (a turning point)
points.structure: Verb て-form + からというもの
points.explanation:
{〜てからというもの} means 'ever since X, things have been (continuously) different'. It is used when a single event became a turning point and the speaker feels a strong, lasting change afterwards — often with a sense of emotion or surprise.

It is stronger and more emotional than plain {〜てから} or {〜て以来[いらい]}. The second half describes an ongoing state or habit, not a one-off action.

**Register:** written and somewhat formal; common in essays, memoirs, interviews and speeches. You can use it in careful speech too, e.g. when telling your life story.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]に来[き]てからというもの、毎日[まいにち]が新[あたら]しい発見[はっけん]の連続[れんぞく]だ。
examples.en: Ever since I came to Japan, every day has been one new discovery after another.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもが生[う]まれてからというもの、夫[おっと]はすっかり早寝[はやね]早起[はやお]きになった。
examples.en: Ever since our child was born, my husband has completely switched to early nights and early mornings.

examples.jp: 祖母[そぼ]が亡[な]くなってからというもの、祖父[そふ]はめっきり口数[くちかず]が減[へ]った。
examples.en: Ever since my grandmother died, my grandfather has become much quieter.

examples.jp: そのウイルスが確認[かくにん]されてからというもの、街[まち]から観光客[かんこうきゃく]の姿[すがた]が消[き]えた。
examples.en: Ever since the virus was detected, tourists have vanished from the streets.

points.notes: Not for a single action: {✕日本[にほん]に来[き]てからというもの、一度[いちど]富士山[ふじさん]に登[のぼ]った} is wrong. The result must be a continuing change.

quiz.q: 禁煙[きんえん]して＿＿、体[からだ]の調子[ちょうし]がとてもいい。
quiz.en: Ever since I quit smoking, I've been feeling really good.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]と出会[であ]って＿＿、彼[かれ]の生活[せいかつ]は一変[いっぺん]した。
quiz.en: Ever since he met her, his life has been completely transformed.

points.title: 〜を皮切[かわき]りに
points.meaning: starting with; beginning with (and then many more)
points.structure: Noun + を皮切[かわき]りに(して) / を皮切[かわき]りとして
points.explanation:
{皮切[かわき]り} originally meant the first moxa burn in a traditional treatment — the first, most painful one. {〜を皮切[かわき]りに} marks X as the starting point of a whole series of similar things that follow: a concert tour, a chain of store openings, a string of revelations.

The second half usually describes expansion or a succession of events ({次々[つぎつぎ]と}, {相次[あいつ]いで}, {全国[ぜんこく]で}).

**Register:** formal; very common in news, press releases and business writing. In speech you might hear it from presenters or announcers.

examples.jp: 来月[らいげつ]の東京[とうきょう]公演[こうえん]を皮切[かわき]りに、全国[ぜんこく]ツアーが始[はじ]まる。
examples.en: Starting with next month's Tokyo show, a nationwide tour will begin.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の発言[はつげん]を皮切[かわき]りに、参加者[さんかしゃ]から次々[つぎつぎ]と意見[いけん]が出[で]た。
examples.en: His remark set things off, and one participant after another voiced an opinion.

examples.jp: 同社[どうしゃ]は大阪店[おおさかてん]を皮切[かわき]りに、海外[かいがい]にも出店[しゅってん]していく方針[ほうしん]だ。
examples.en: Beginning with its Osaka store, the company plans to open branches overseas as well.

examples.jp: この発見[はっけん]を皮切[かわき]りとして、新[あら]たな研究[けんきゅう]が相次[あいつ]いだ。
examples.en: This discovery was the first of a wave of new studies.

points.notes: Compare {〜を限[かぎ]りに} (next point), which marks an end point, and {〜を境[さかい]に}, which marks a turning point between 'before' and 'after'.

quiz.q: 新作[しんさく]映画[えいが]は、ニューヨーク＿＿世界[せかい]十[じゅっ]か国[こく]で公開[こうかい]される。
quiz.en: The new film will open in ten countries around the world, starting with New York.

quiz.q: 一人[ひとり]の社員[しゃいん]の告発[こくはつ]＿＿、会社[かいしゃ]の不正[ふせい]が次々[つぎつぎ]と明[あき]らかになった。
quiz.en: Starting with one employee's whistle-blowing, the company's wrongdoings came to light one after another.

points.title: 〜を限[かぎ]りに
points.meaning: as of (and no longer after); with ... as the last
points.structure: Noun (time) + を限[かぎ]りに
points.explanation:
{〜を限[かぎ]りに} marks the last moment something continues: after this point, it stops. It often comes with time words like {今日[きょう]}, {本日[ほんじつ]}, {今月[こんげつ]末[まつ]} or {今[こん]シーズン}, and the second half talks about quitting, closing, retiring or ending.

A separate fixed phrase, {声[こえ]を限[かぎ]りに}, means 'at the top of one's voice' — literally 'to the limit of one's voice'.

**Register:** formal. You will see it on shop notices ('closing as of the end of this month'), in retirement announcements and in news. It also works in serious speech: {今日[きょう]を限[かぎ]りにお酒[さけ]をやめる}.

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]を限[かぎ]りに、タバコをやめることにした。
examples.en: I've decided that today is my last day of smoking.

examples.jp: 当店[とうてん]は今月末[こんげつまつ]を限[かぎ]りに閉店[へいてん]いたします。
examples.en: This shop will close permanently at the end of this month.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は今[こん]シーズンを限[かぎ]りに、現役[げんえき]を引退[いんたい]すると発表[はっぴょう]した。
examples.en: He announced that he will retire from competition at the end of this season.

examples.jp: 遭難者[そうなんしゃ]は声[こえ]を限[かぎ]りに助[たす]けを求[もと]めた。
examples.en: The stranded climber cried for help at the top of his voice.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {〜限[かぎ]り} 'as long as / as far as' ({私[わたし]の知[し]る限[かぎ]り} 'as far as I know') or {〜に限[かぎ]り} 'only, limited to' ({本日[ほんじつ]に限[かぎ]り半額[はんがく]} 'half price today only').

quiz.q: 本日[ほんじつ]＿＿、この番組[ばんぐみ]は終了[しゅうりょう]となります。
quiz.en: With today's broadcast, this programme comes to an end.

quiz.q: 三十年[さんじゅうねん]続[つづ]いたこの商店[しょうてん]も、今年[ことし]＿＿店[みせ]を閉[し]めることになった。
quiz.en: This shop, which has been running for thirty years, will close for good at the end of this year.

units.title: Doing two things at once, and 'although'
units.summary: Ways to combine a main activity with a side one ({かたわら}, {がてら}, {かたがた}), back-and-forth actions ({〜つ〜つ}), and concessive 'while/although' patterns used in polite and written Japanese.

points.title: 〜かたがた
points.meaning: while also; by way of; combining X with Y
points.structure: Noun (often a する-noun) + かたがた
points.explanation:
{〜かたがた} means 'doing X and at the same time using the occasion for Y'. In practice it lives inside a handful of polite set phrases: {お礼[れい]かたがた} (to thank you, and also...), {ご挨拶[あいさつ]かたがた} (as a greeting, and also...), {お見舞[みま]いかたがた} (visiting someone sick, and also...).

The second half is usually a visit or a report: {伺[うかが]う}, {訪[たず]ねる}, {ご報告[ほうこく]する}.

**Register:** very formal, mostly business letters, emails and formal visits. Outside those set phrases it sounds stiff. In daily life you'd use {がてら} or {ついでに} instead.

examples.jp: 散歩[さんぽ]かたがた、近所[きんじょ]の本屋[ほんや]をのぞいてきた。
examples.en: I went for a walk and popped into the local bookshop while I was at it.

examples.jp: 先日[せんじつ]のお礼[れい]かたがた、ご挨拶[あいさつ]に伺[うかが]いました。
examples.en: I've come to say hello, and also to thank you for the other day.

examples.jp: 出張[しゅっちょう]かたがた、大阪[おおさか]に住[す]む旧友[きゅうゆう]を訪[たず]ねた。
examples.en: While on a business trip, I took the chance to visit an old friend in Osaka.

examples.jp: 略儀[りゃくぎ]ながら、書中[しょちゅう]をもってお礼[れい]かたがたご報告[ほうこく]申[もう]し上[あ]げます。
examples.en: Though this is an informal way to do so, I write to report to you and to express my thanks.

points.notes: The last example is a standard closing line in formal Japanese letters — worth memorising whole. Unlike {かたわら}, {かたがた} attaches directly to the noun without {の}.

quiz.q: 入院中[にゅういんちゅう]の部長[ぶちょう]のお見舞[みま]い＿＿、仕事[しごと]の報告[ほうこく]に行[い]った。
quiz.en: I visited the department head in hospital, and reported on work while I was there.

quiz.q: 先日[せんじつ]のお礼[れい]＿＿、近況[きんきょう]をご報告[ほうこく]いたします。
quiz.en: I'm writing to thank you for the other day, and also to let you know how I've been.

points.title: 〜かたわら
points.meaning: while (doing one's main job), also (doing something else)
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + かたわら / Noun + の + かたわら
points.explanation:
{かたわら} literally means 'beside'. As grammar, {X かたわら Y} describes someone's life over a long period: X is their main occupation, and on the side they also do Y. Think 'a company employee who writes novels on the side'.

It is about ongoing roles or long-term activities, not two things happening at the same moment (for that, use {〜ながら}).

**Register:** written. Common in biographies, profiles, news features and author introductions. In conversation people tend to say {〜しながら} or {〜の他[ほか]に} instead.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は会社[かいしゃ]に勤[つと]めるかたわら、小説[しょうせつ]を書[か]いている。
examples.en: He works for a company and writes novels on the side.

examples.jp: 母[はは]は子育[こそだ]てのかたわら、大学院[だいがくいん]で研究[けんきゅう]を続[つづ]けた。
examples.en: While raising children, my mother continued her research in graduate school.

examples.jp: その医師[いし]は診療[しんりょう]のかたわら、地域[ちいき]のボランティア活動[かつどう]にも力[ちから]を入[い]れている。
examples.en: Alongside seeing patients, the doctor also puts a lot into community volunteer work.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は翻訳[ほんやく]の仕事[しごと]をするかたわら、日本語[にほんご]教師[きょうし]としても活躍[かつやく]している。
examples.en: Besides working as a translator, she is also active as a Japanese teacher.

points.notes: {かたわら} = long-term double life; {がてら} = one outing serving two purposes; {ながら} = two actions at the same moment.

quiz.q: 父[ちち]は農業[のうぎょう]を営[いとな]む＿＿、町議会[ちょうぎかい]議員[ぎいん]も務[つと]めている。
quiz.en: My father runs a farm and also serves as a town councillor.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は大学[だいがく]で教[おし]える＿＿、作曲家[さっきょくか]としても活動[かつどう]している。
quiz.en: Besides teaching at a university, he is also active as a composer.

points.title: 〜がてら
points.meaning: while (out doing X), also; taking the opportunity
points.structure: Verb ます-stem / Noun (often a する-noun) + がてら
points.explanation:
{〜がてら} means doing X and using that same outing to do Y as well. Typically the second half involves going somewhere: {歩[ある]く}, {行[い]く}, {寄[よ]る}, {出[で]かける}. 'I'll go to the convenience store while I'm out for a walk.'

It describes one occasion, not a long-term double life (that's {かたわら}).

**Register:** neutral to slightly formal, and genuinely used in conversation — more common in real life than most points in this unit. {散歩[さんぽ]がてら} and {買[か]い物[もの]がてら} are especially frequent.

examples.jp: 散歩[さんぽ]がてら、コンビニに寄[よ]ってきます。
examples.en: I'll stop by the convenience store while I'm out for a walk.

examples.jp: 運動[うんどう]がてら、一駅[ひとえき]手前[てまえ]で降[お]りて歩[ある]くことにしている。
examples.en: For the exercise, I make a habit of getting off one stop early and walking.

examples.jp: 買[か]い物[もの]がてら、友達[ともだち]を駅[えき]まで送[おく]っていった。
examples.en: I was going shopping anyway, so I walked my friend to the station.

examples.jp: 桜[さくら]を見[み]がてら、川沿[かわぞ]いの道[みち]をのんびり歩[ある]いた。
examples.en: I strolled along the riverside path, enjoying the cherry blossoms as I went.

points.notes: {ついでに} is the everyday equivalent, but it puts the focus on the second action as an incidental extra; {がてら} gives both actions roughly equal weight.

quiz.q: 気分[きぶん]転換[てんかん]＿＿、近[ちか]くの公園[こうえん]まで歩[ある]いてきた。
quiz.en: I walked to the nearby park for a change of scenery.

quiz.q: 京都[きょうと]に住[す]む友人[ゆうじん]に会[あ]い＿＿、紅葉[こうよう]を見[み]に行[い]った。
quiz.en: I went to see the autumn leaves, and visited a friend who lives in Kyoto while I was there.

points.title: 〜つ〜つ
points.meaning: back and forth; alternately; mutually
points.structure: Verb₁ ます-stem + つ + Verb₂ ます-stem + つ
points.explanation:
{〜つ〜つ} pairs two verbs — usually a verb and its passive, or two opposites — to show actions alternating back and forth. It is a classical leftover, so it is not productive: you only use it with a small set of fixed expressions.

- {持[も]ちつ持[も]たれつ} — give and take, mutual help
- {抜[ぬ]きつ抜[ぬ]かれつ} — overtaking and being overtaken (a close race)
- {追[お]いつ追[お]われつ} — chasing and being chased (neck and neck)
- {行[い]きつ戻[もど]りつ} — pacing back and forth

**Register:** literary, but {持[も]ちつ持[も]たれつ} is a well-known saying used in everyday speech, and sports reports love {抜[ぬ]きつ抜[ぬ]かれつ}.

examples.jp: 世[よ]の中[なか]は持[も]ちつ持[も]たれつだ。
examples.en: Life is all about give and take.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は彼女[かのじょ]の家[いえ]の前[まえ]を行[い]きつ戻[もど]りつしていた。
examples.en: He was pacing back and forth in front of her house.

examples.jp: 二台[にだい]の車[くるま]は抜[ぬ]きつ抜[ぬ]かれつのレースを繰[く]り広[ひろ]げた。
examples.en: The two cars fought a race in which they kept overtaking each other.

examples.jp: 両[りょう]チームは追[お]いつ追[お]われつの接戦[せっせん]を演[えん]じた。
examples.en: The two teams played a neck-and-neck game.

points.notes: Don't invent new pairs; learn the fixed ones. {〜つ〜つ} works as a noun with {の} ({抜[ぬ]きつ抜[ぬ]かれつのレース}) or as a verb with {する} ({行[い]きつ戻[もど]りつする}).

quiz.q: ゴール直前[ちょくぜん]まで、二人[ふたり]のランナーは抜[ぬ]き＿＿抜[ぬ]かれつの争[あらそ]いを続[つづ]けた。
quiz.en: Right up to the finish line, the two runners kept overtaking each other.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は告白[こくはく]しようか迷[まよ]って、廊下[ろうか]を行[い]きつ＿＿していた。
quiz.en: Unable to decide whether to confess his feelings, he paced back and forth in the corridor.

points.title: 〜ながらも
points.meaning: although; while (admittedly); despite being
points.structure: Verb ます-stem / い-adj / な-adj stem / Noun + ながらも
points.explanation:
You know {〜ながら} as 'while doing'. With states (adjectives, nouns, verbs like {知[し]る}, {いる}) it can also mean 'although', and adding {も} makes this concessive meaning unmistakable: {狭[せま]いながらも} 'small though it is'.

The pattern is 'X is true, but (surprisingly / nevertheless) Y'. It often expresses quiet admiration: small but cosy, young but capable, complaining but helping anyway.

**Register:** more written than spoken, but common: essays, reviews, news, and polite speech. Fixed phrases like {残念[ざんねん]ながら} and {狭[せま]いながらも楽[たの]しい我[わ]が家[や]} are part of everyday language.

examples.jp: 狭[せま]いながらも楽[たの]しい我[わ]が家[や]。
examples.en: Our home may be small, but it's a happy one.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は文句[もんく]を言[い]いながらも、最後[さいご]まで手伝[てつだ]ってくれた。
examples.en: He grumbled, but he helped me right to the end.

examples.jp: 少[すこ]しずつながらも、売[う]り上[あ]げは回復[かいふく]しつつある。
examples.en: Slowly but surely, sales are recovering.

examples.jp: その小説[しょうせつ]は短編[たんぺん]ながらも、読[よ]む者[もの]に深[ふか]い感動[かんどう]を与[あた]える。
examples.en: Though only a short story, the work moves its readers deeply.

points.notes: Similar: {〜つつも} (Verb stem only, more written) and {〜にもかかわらず} (more objective, used for facts). {〜ながらも} often carries the speaker's personal evaluation.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]は体調[たいちょう]が悪[わる]い＿＿、最後[さいご]まで笑顔[えがお]で舞台[ぶたい]に立[た]ち続[つづ]けた。
quiz.en: Although she was feeling unwell, she stayed on stage smiling until the very end.

quiz.q: 子[こ]ども＿＿、彼[かれ]の意見[いけん]には説得力[せっとくりょく]があった。
quiz.en: Although he was a child, his opinion was persuasive.

points.title: 〜ところを
points.meaning: although (you are in the middle of / it's a bad time); just as
points.structure: Verb / い-adj (plain) + ところを / Noun + の + ところを
points.explanation:
{〜ところを} has two main uses.

**1. Polite apology or thanks.** 'In a situation where X (you're busy / resting / should be doing otherwise), you nevertheless did Y for me.' This is extremely common in business: {お忙[いそが]しいところを申[もう]し訳[わけ]ありません}, {お休[やす]みのところを失礼[しつれい]します}.

**2. Caught in the act.** 'Just as X was happening, (someone) did something to them' — usually with a passive or verbs like {見[み]つかる}, {捕[つか]まる}, {助[たす]ける}: {逃[に]げるところを捕[つか]まった}.

**Register:** use 1 is one of the most useful N1 patterns for working in Japan — you will hear and say it daily in emails and phone calls. Use 2 is common in news and narratives.

examples.jp: お忙[いそが]しいところを、わざわざお越[こ]しいただきありがとうございます。
examples.en: Thank you for taking the time to come, busy as you are.

examples.jp: お休[やす]みのところを、突然[とつぜん]お電話[でんわ]して申[もう]し訳[わけ]ありません。
examples.en: I'm sorry to call you out of the blue on your day off.

examples.jp: 犯人[はんにん]は店[みせ]から出[で]てきたところを逮捕[たいほ]された。
examples.en: The culprit was arrested just as he came out of the shop.

examples.jp: 本来[ほんらい]なら私[わたし]が伺[うかが]うべきところを、ご足労[そくろう]いただき恐縮[きょうしゅく]です。
examples.en: I really ought to have come to you; I'm very grateful that you made the trip here instead.

points.notes: In casual or less formal speech the {を} is often dropped: {お忙[いそが]しいところすみません}. Don't confuse with {ところに/ところへ} 'just when (something/someone arrived)' or {ところで} 'even if'.

quiz.q: お疲[つか]れの＿＿、遅[おそ]くまでお付[つ]き合[あ]いいただき、ありがとうございました。
quiz.en: Thank you for staying with us so late when you must be tired.

quiz.q: 万引[まんび]きをしようとしている＿＿、店員[てんいん]に見[み]つかった。
quiz.en: He was spotted by a shop assistant just as he was about to shoplift.

points.title: 〜ながらに
points.meaning: while still; as (one) is; from (birth); unchanged since
points.structure: Noun / Verb ます-stem + ながらに(して) / ながらの + Noun
points.explanation:
{〜ながらに} means 'in the state of X, with X unchanged'. Like {〜つ〜つ}, it lives in a small number of fixed expressions:

- {涙[なみだ]ながらに} — in tears, tearfully
- {生[う]まれながらに(して)} — from birth, innately
- {いながらにして} — without leaving (home, etc.)
- {昔[むかし]ながらの} — old-fashioned, traditional, unchanged since long ago

**Register:** written and formal, but {昔[むかし]ながらの} is everywhere in everyday Japanese — on shop signs, food packaging and travel guides. {涙[なみだ]ながらに} is a staple of news reports about press conferences and court cases.

examples.jp: この町[まち]には昔[むかし]ながらの町並[まちな]みが残[のこ]っている。
examples.en: This town still has its traditional streetscape.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は涙[なみだ]ながらに、事故[じこ]の様子[ようす]を語[かた]った。
examples.en: In tears, she described what happened in the accident.

examples.jp: 人[ひと]は生[う]まれながらにして平等[びょうどう]である。
examples.en: All people are born equal.

examples.jp: インターネットのおかげで、家[いえ]にいながらにして世界中[せかいじゅう]の映画[えいが]が見[み]られる。
examples.en: Thanks to the internet, you can watch films from all over the world without leaving your home.

points.notes: Different from concessive {〜ながらも} 'although'. {〜ながらに} is not concessive; it describes the state in which something is done.

quiz.q: 被害者[ひがいしゃ]の母親[ははおや]は涙[なみだ]＿＿犯人[はんにん]への思[おも]いを訴[うった]えた。
quiz.en: The victim's mother tearfully spoke of her feelings toward the perpetrator.

quiz.q: この店[みせ]では、昔[むかし]＿＿製法[せいほう]で豆腐[とうふ]を作[つく]っている。
quiz.en: At this shop, tofu is made using the traditional method.

units.title: Extremes of feeling
units.summary: Formal ways to say 'extremely', 'utterly' and 'I can't help feeling', from {失礼[しつれい]極[きわ]まりない} to {光栄[こうえい]の至[いた]り} and {感謝[かんしゃ]に堪[た]えません}.

points.title: 〜極[きわ]まりない／〜極[きわ]まる
points.meaning: extremely; utterly (usually negative)
points.structure: な-adj stem + 極[きわ]まりない / 極[きわ]まる
points.explanation:
{極[きわ]まる} means 'to reach the extreme'. Attached to a na-adjective, {〜極[きわ]まりない} and {〜極[きわ]まる} both mean 'as X as it gets' — {極[きわ]まりない} is literally 'has no limit'. Despite one looking negative, they mean the same thing.

The adjectives are usually negative judgements: {失礼[しつれい]}, {危険[きけん]}, {不愉快[ふゆかい]}, {非常識[ひじょうしき]}, {不誠実[ふせいじつ]}, {退屈[たいくつ]}. The speaker is condemning something.

**Register:** formal and written — editorials, criticism, official complaints. In speech it sounds indignant and stiff, but you will hear {失礼[しつれい]極[きわ]まりない} from angry people on TV dramas.

examples.jp: あの店員[てんいん]の態度[たいど]は失礼[しつれい]極[きわ]まりない。
examples.en: That shop assistant's attitude is incredibly rude.

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]の夜[よる]に無灯火[むとうか]で自転車[じてんしゃ]に乗[の]るのは危険[きけん]極[きわ]まりない。
examples.en: Riding a bike without a light on a rainy night is extremely dangerous.

examples.jp: 連絡[れんらく]もなく約束[やくそく]を破[やぶ]るとは、非常識[ひじょうしき]極[きわ]まる行為[こうい]だ。
examples.en: Breaking a promise without even getting in touch is utterly inconsiderate behaviour.

examples.jp: 政府[せいふ]の対応[たいおう]は不誠実[ふせいじつ]極[きわ]まりないと、野党[やとう]は強[つよ]く批判[ひはん]した。
examples.en: The opposition strongly criticised the government's response as utterly insincere.

points.notes: Fixed expression: {感[かん]極[きわ]まる} 'to be overcome with emotion' ({感[かん]極[きわ]まって泣[な]き出[だ]す}). Compare {〜の極[きわ]み} (after nouns, with {の}).

quiz.q: 酔[よ]って運転[うんてん]するなど、危険[きけん]＿＿。
quiz.en: Driving drunk is extremely dangerous.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]の言動[げんどう]は不愉快[ふゆかい]＿＿ものだった。
quiz.en: His words and behaviour were extremely unpleasant.

points.title: 〜の至[いた]り
points.meaning: the utmost; extremely (in fixed polite phrases)
points.structure: Noun + の至[いた]り(だ／です)
points.explanation:
{至[いた]り} means 'the furthest point reached'. {〜の至[いた]り} is used in a small set of fixed phrases, mostly polite expressions of honour, gratitude or embarrassment:

- {光栄[こうえい]の至[いた]り} — a great honour
- {恐縮[きょうしゅく]の至[いた]り} — I'm deeply obliged / terribly sorry
- {感激[かんげき]の至[いた]り} — deeply moved
- {赤面[せきめん]の至[いた]り} — utterly embarrassing
- {若気[わかげ]の至[いた]り} — youthful folly (a mistake you made because you were young)

**Register:** very formal speeches and letters, except {若気[わかげ]の至[いた]り}, which is a common everyday idiom, often used with a wry smile about your teenage self.

examples.jp: このような賞[しょう]をいただき、光栄[こうえい]の至[いた]りです。
examples.en: It is a great honour to receive such an award.

examples.jp: あんな派手[はで]な服[ふく]を着[き]ていたのは、若気[わかげ]の至[いた]りだった。
examples.en: Wearing such flashy clothes was just youthful folly.

examples.jp: 人前[ひとまえ]で名前[なまえ]を間違[まちが]えるとは、まったく赤面[せきめん]の至[いた]りです。
examples.en: Getting someone's name wrong in public — I'm thoroughly embarrassed.

examples.jp: 皆様[みなさま]にご迷惑[めいわく]をおかけし、恐縮[きょうしゅく]の至[いた]りでございます。
examples.en: I am deeply sorry for the trouble I have caused you all.

points.notes: Don't make your own combinations; stick to the set phrases. {〜の極[きわ]み} is broader and combines with more nouns.

quiz.q: 名誉[めいよ]ある賞[しょう]を受賞[じゅしょう]し、光栄[こうえい]＿＿です。
quiz.en: Winning such a prestigious prize is a great honour.

quiz.q: 学生[がくせい]時代[じだい]に髪[かみ]を金色[きんいろ]に染[そ]めたのは、若気[わかげ]の＿＿だ。
quiz.en: Dyeing my hair gold as a student was youthful folly.

points.title: 〜の極[きわ]み
points.meaning: the height of; the ultimate in
points.structure: Noun + の極[きわ]み
points.explanation:
{極[きわ]み} is the noun 'extreme, peak'. {X の極[きわ]み} means 'the very height of X' and works with both positive and negative nouns: {贅沢[ぜいたく]の極[きわ]み} (the height of luxury), {疲労[ひろう]の極[きわ]み} (utter exhaustion), {無責任[むせきにん]の極[きわ]み} (the height of irresponsibility), {痛恨[つうこん]の極[きわ]み} (deepest regret).

{痛恨[つうこん]の極[きわ]み} is a cliché in formal apologies and post-match interviews. {感激[かんげき]の極[きわ]み} expresses overwhelming emotion.

**Register:** formal and written, though it appears in speech for emphasis and in advertising ('the ultimate in comfort').

examples.jp: 一流[いちりゅう]ホテルのスイートルームに泊[と]まるなんて、贅沢[ぜいたく]の極[きわ]みだ。
examples.en: Staying in a suite at a top hotel is the height of luxury.

examples.jp: 決勝[けっしょう]で負[ま]けたことは、痛恨[つうこん]の極[きわ]みです。
examples.en: Losing in the final is a matter of the deepest regret.

examples.jp: 徹夜[てつや]が三日[みっか]続[つづ]き、疲労[ひろう]の極[きわ]みに達[たっ]した。
examples.en: After three all-nighters in a row, I reached the point of utter exhaustion.

examples.jp: 事故[じこ]の責任[せきにん]を部下[ぶか]に押[お]し付[つ]けるとは、無責任[むせきにん]の極[きわ]みだ。
examples.en: Pushing the blame for the accident onto his subordinates is the height of irresponsibility.

points.notes: {〜極[きわ]まりない} attaches directly to na-adjectives ({失礼[しつれい]極[きわ]まりない}); {〜の極[きわ]み} needs {の} and a noun.

quiz.q: 世界一[せかいいち]の山[やま]の頂上[ちょうじょう]に立[た]てたのは、感激[かんげき]＿＿だった。
quiz.en: Standing on the summit of the world's highest mountain was the most moving experience imaginable.

quiz.q: 自分[じぶん]の失敗[しっぱい]を他人[たにん]のせいにするとは、無責任[むせきにん]の＿＿だ。
quiz.en: Blaming others for your own failure is the height of irresponsibility.

points.title: 〜といったらない
points.meaning: indescribably; words can't express how (X) it is
points.structure: Noun / い-adj + さ (noun form) + といったらない／ったらない
points.explanation:
{〜といったらない} literally says 'if you try to name X, there is nothing (that compares)'. It means that a feeling or quality is so intense it is beyond words: {悔[くや]しさといったらない} 'I can't tell you how frustrating it was'.

It usually comes after a noun made from an adjective with {さ}: {美[うつく]しさ}, {寂[さび]しさ}, {恥[は]ずかしさ}, {しつこさ}. It can be positive or negative. When talking about the past, use {〜といったらなかった}.

**Register:** unlike most of this unit, this one is genuinely used in conversation, especially the contracted {〜ったらない}. It also appears in essays and novels.

examples.jp: あの人[ひと]のしつこさったらないよ。
examples.en: You can't believe how pushy that guy is.

examples.jp: 大勢[おおぜい]の前[まえ]で転[ころ]んだ時[とき]の恥[は]ずかしさといったらなかった。
examples.en: I can't describe how embarrassed I was when I fell over in front of all those people.

examples.jp: 一人[ひとり]で暮[く]らし始[はじ]めた頃[ころ]の寂[さび]しさといったらなかった。
examples.en: When I first started living alone, I was lonelier than I can say.

examples.jp: 初[はじ]めて山頂[さんちょう]から見[み]た朝日[あさひ]の美[うつく]しさといったらなかった。
examples.en: The beauty of the sunrise I saw from the summit for the first time was beyond words.

points.notes: A negative-only variant is {〜といったらありはしない／ありゃしない}: {面倒[めんどう]くさいったらありゃしない} 'what a pain'. Don't confuse with {〜といったら} 'speaking of', as in {日本[にほん]料理[りょうり]といったら寿司[すし]だ}.

quiz.q: 合格[ごうかく]の知[し]らせを聞[き]いた時[とき]のうれしさ＿＿。
quiz.en: I can't tell you how happy I was when I heard I'd passed.

quiz.q: 夜中[よなか]に一人[ひとり]で墓地[ぼち]を歩[ある]いた時[とき]の怖[こわ]さ＿＿なかった。
quiz.en: Walking through the graveyard alone at midnight was more frightening than I can describe.

points.title: 〜てやまない
points.meaning: never stop (hoping / loving etc.); sincerely, deeply
points.structure: Verb て-form + やまない
points.explanation:
{やむ} means 'to stop, cease' (like rain stopping). {〜てやまない} means a feeling continues without end: 'I cannot stop hoping', i.e. 'I sincerely hope'. It combines only with verbs of deep feeling: {願[ねが]う}, {祈[いの]る}, {望[のぞ]む}, {愛[あい]する}, {尊敬[そんけい]する}, {期待[きたい]する}, {憧[あこが]れる}.

When it describes the speaker, it's used in formal speeches, wedding toasts and letters: {ご活躍[かつやく]を祈[いの]ってやみません}. It also describes other people's lifelong devotion in biographies.

**Register:** formal, ceremonial and written. Not for casual feelings — {✕ラーメンを食[た]べたくてやまない} is wrong.

examples.jp: 世界[せかい]の平和[へいわ]を祈[いの]ってやまない。
examples.en: I pray with all my heart for world peace.

examples.jp: 皆様[みなさま]のご健康[けんこう]とご活躍[かつやく]を願[ねが]ってやみません。
examples.en: I sincerely wish you all good health and continued success.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は生涯[しょうがい]、故郷[こきょう]を愛[あい]してやまなかった。
examples.en: All his life he never stopped loving his hometown.

examples.jp: 私[わたし]が尊敬[そんけい]してやまない恩師[おんし]が、この春[はる]退職[たいしょく]された。
examples.en: My former teacher, whom I deeply admire, retired this spring.

points.notes: Compare {〜てならない／〜てたまらない} 'can't help feeling', which express strong spontaneous feelings ({心配[しんぱい]でならない}). {〜てやまない} is about a lasting, sincere wish or devotion.

quiz.q: 新郎[しんろう]新婦[しんぷ]のお二人[ふたり]の末永[すえなが]い幸[しあわ]せを願[ねが]って＿＿。
quiz.en: I sincerely wish the bride and groom lasting happiness.

quiz.q: 子[こ]どもの頃[ころ]から私[わたし]が憧[あこが]れて＿＿のは、宇宙[うちゅう]飛行士[ひこうし]という仕事[しごと]だ。
quiz.en: The job I have always longed for since childhood is that of an astronaut.

points.title: 〜を禁[きん]じ得[え]ない
points.meaning: can't help feeling; can't suppress
points.structure: Noun (emotion) + を禁[きん]じ得[え]ない
points.explanation:
{禁[きん]じる} is 'to prohibit' and {得[え]ない} is 'cannot'. So {〜を禁[きん]じ得[え]ない} means 'I cannot prevent (this feeling) from arising': I can't help feeling anger, sympathy, surprise, or can't hold back tears.

Nouns that commonly appear: {怒[いか]り}, {同情[どうじょう]}, {驚[おどろ]き}, {涙[なみだ]}, {失望[しつぼう]}, {憤[いきどお]り}, {戸惑[とまど]い}. The feeling is usually triggered by something the speaker has witnessed or heard about.

**Register:** very formal, written — editorials, statements, essays, formal speeches. In conversation you'd say {〜せずにはいられない} or just {本当[ほんとう]に腹[はら]が立[た]つ}.

examples.jp: 突然[とつぜん]の訃報[ふほう]に、驚[おどろ]きを禁[きん]じ得[え]なかった。
examples.en: I could not help being shocked by the sudden news of his death.

examples.jp: 家族[かぞく]を失[うしな]った子[こ]どもたちの姿[すがた]には、同情[どうじょう]を禁[きん]じ得[え]ない。
examples.en: One cannot help but feel sympathy for the children who lost their families.

examples.jp: 被害者[ひがいしゃ]の話[はなし]を聞[き]き、犯人[はんにん]への怒[いか]りを禁[きん]じ得[え]ない。
examples.en: Hearing the victim's story, I cannot suppress my anger at the perpetrator.

examples.jp: 一部[いちぶ]の政治家[せいじか]の無責任[むせきにん]な発言[はつげん]には、失望[しつぼう]を禁[きん]じ得[え]ない。
examples.en: I cannot hide my disappointment at the irresponsible remarks of certain politicians.

points.notes: Only nouns for emotions or tears. It is not used for actions: {✕笑[わら]うことを禁[きん]じ得[え]ない}; use {笑[わら]わずにはいられない} instead.

quiz.q: 戦争[せんそう]の写真[しゃしん]を見[み]て、涙[なみだ]＿＿。
quiz.en: Looking at the war photographs, I could not hold back my tears.
choices: を余儀[よぎ]なくされた
を禁[きん]じ得[え]なかった

quiz.q: 長年[ながねん]信頼[しんらい]してきた友人[ゆうじん]の裏切[うらぎ]りに、怒[いか]り＿＿禁[きん]じ得[え]ない。
quiz.en: I cannot suppress my anger at the betrayal of a friend I had trusted for years.

points.title: 〜に堪[た]えない
points.meaning: (1) too awful to (watch/listen to); (2) extremely, deeply (grateful, regretful)
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form: 見[み]る／聞[き]く) + に堪[た]えない / Noun (感謝[かんしゃ]・遺憾[いかん] etc.) + に堪[た]えない
points.explanation:
{堪[た]える} means 'to bear, to stand'. {〜に堪[た]えない} has two separate uses:

**1. After {見[み]る}, {聞[き]く}, {読[よ]む}:** 'so bad you can't bear to watch/hear/read it'. {見[み]るに堪[た]えない} 'unwatchable', {聞[き]くに堪[た]えない悪口[わるくち]} 'abuse too vile to listen to'.

**2. After a feeling noun:** 'I cannot contain (this feeling)' = extremely. Mainly {感謝[かんしゃ]に堪[た]えない} 'deeply grateful', {遺憾[いかん]に堪[た]えない} 'deeply regrettable', {憂慮[ゆうりょ]に堪[た]えない} 'gravely concerned'.

**Register:** both are formal and written. Use 2 is typical of speeches and official statements. The JLPT often writes it in hiragana: {にたえない}.

examples.jp: 最近[さいきん]のテレビ番組[ばんぐみ]には、見[み]るに堪[た]えないものが多[おお]い。
examples.en: A lot of TV programmes these days are unwatchable.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]らの口論[こうろん]は聞[き]くに堪[た]えないほどひどかった。
examples.en: Their argument was so nasty it was unbearable to listen to.

examples.jp: 皆様[みなさま]の温[あたた]かいご支援[しえん]に、感謝[かんしゃ]に堪[た]えません。
examples.en: I am deeply grateful for your warm support.

examples.jp: 今回[こんかい]の事態[じたい]は、誠[まこと]に遺憾[いかん]に堪[た]えない。
examples.en: This situation is truly and deeply regrettable.

points.notes: Its positive counterpart {〜に堪[た]える} 'worth / able to withstand' is the next point.

quiz.q: 事故[じこ]現場[げんば]の様子[ようす]は、見[み]る＿＿ものだった。
quiz.en: The scene of the accident was too horrible to look at.

quiz.q: 多[おお]くの方々[かたがた]からご支援[しえん]をいただき、感謝[かんしゃ]＿＿。
quiz.en: I am deeply grateful to have received support from so many people.
choices: を余儀[よぎ]なくされます

points.title: 〜に堪[た]える
points.meaning: worth (doing); good enough to; able to withstand
points.structure: Noun / Verb (dictionary form) + に堪[た]える
points.explanation:
The positive form {〜に堪[た]える} means something is good enough to stand up to a certain use or scrutiny: {鑑賞[かんしょう]に堪[た]える} 'worth watching (for adults/experts)', {読[よ]むに堪[た]える} 'worth reading', {批判[ひはん]に堪[た]える} 'able to withstand criticism'.

With physical hardship ({寒[さむ]さ}, {重[おも]さ}, {長時間[ちょうじかん]の手術[しゅじゅつ]}), the kanji {耐[た]える} 'endure' is usually used instead, but the grammar is the same.

**Register:** written — reviews, criticism, essays. It often appears with {十分[じゅうぶん]} or {だけの}: {専門家[せんもんか]の目[め]に十分[じゅうぶん]堪[た]える}.

examples.jp: この作品[さくひん]は、大人[おとな]の鑑賞[かんしょう]にも十分[じゅうぶん]堪[た]える。
examples.en: This work is quite good enough for adult audiences too.

examples.jp: 読[よ]むに堪[た]える翻訳[ほんやく]は、意外[いがい]に少[すく]ない。
examples.en: Translations that are actually worth reading are surprisingly few.

examples.jp: 高齢[こうれい]の父[ちち]には、長時間[ちょうじかん]の手術[しゅじゅつ]に耐[た]える体力[たいりょく]がない。
examples.en: My elderly father doesn't have the strength to withstand a long operation.

examples.jp: 素人[しろうと]の論文[ろんぶん]だが、専門家[せんもんか]の批判[ひはん]に堪[た]えるだけの内容[ないよう]がある。
examples.en: It's an amateur's paper, but its content can stand up to expert criticism.

points.notes: Compare {〜に足[た]る} 'worthy of' (Unit 9), which is about deserving trust or attention; {〜に堪[た]える} is about standing up to use or scrutiny.

quiz.q: この映画[えいが]は子[こ]ども向[む]けだが、大人[おとな]の鑑賞[かんしょう]に＿＿作品[さくひん]だ。
quiz.en: This film is aimed at children, but it's good enough for adults to enjoy too.

quiz.q: 長年[ながねん]の風雪[ふうせつ]に＿＿きた古[ふる]い寺[てら]が、地震[じしん]で倒壊[とうかい]した。
quiz.en: The old temple, which had withstood wind and snow for many years, collapsed in the earthquake.

units.title: Only with X — and without X
units.summary: Expressing what something depends on: prerequisites ({あっての}, {なくしては}, {ことなしに}), 'nobody but X' ({をおいて}), 'depending on / regardless of' ({いかん}) and 'if it's for X' ({とあれば}).

points.title: 〜あっての
points.meaning: Y exists only because of X; Y is unthinkable without X
points.structure: Noun₁ + あっての + Noun₂
points.explanation:
{X あっての Y} means 'Y is possible only because X exists'. It stresses that X is the essential foundation of Y, and often carries a sense of gratitude or a reminder of priorities.

The classic example is the business motto {お客様[きゃくさま]あっての商売[しょうばい]} — 'a business only exists thanks to its customers'. You'll also hear {〜あってのことです} in speeches when thanking people: 'this was only possible thanks to ...'.

**Register:** formal but genuinely used — in business, speeches, interviews and sports comments. Not difficult once you notice it.

examples.jp: 健康[けんこう]あっての人生[じんせい]だ。無理[むり]はしないほうがいい。
examples.en: Without your health you have nothing. Don't overdo it.

examples.jp: お客様[きゃくさま]あっての商売[しょうばい]だから、サービスには手[て]を抜[ぬ]けない。
examples.en: A business depends on its customers, so we can't cut corners on service.

examples.jp: ファンの皆様[みなさま]の応援[おうえん]あっての優勝[ゆうしょう]でした。
examples.en: We could only have won the championship with the support of our fans.

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]の私[わたし]があるのは、恩師[おんし]の指導[しどう]あってのことです。
examples.en: I owe who I am today entirely to my teacher's guidance.

points.notes: Close in meaning to {〜があってこそ}. Note the structure: {あっての} links two nouns, so the second noun (or {こと}) must follow.

quiz.q: 選手[せんしゅ]＿＿チームだ。一人[ひとり]ひとりを大切[たいせつ]にしなければならない。
quiz.en: A team is nothing without its players. We must value each one of them.

quiz.q: 社員[しゃいん]の努力[どりょく]＿＿今回[こんかい]の成功[せいこう]です。
quiz.en: This success was only possible thanks to our employees' hard work.

points.title: 〜なくして(は)
points.meaning: without X, (Y is impossible)
points.structure: Noun + なくして(は) + negative / impossible
points.explanation:
{〜なくして(は)} means 'without X', and the second half says something cannot happen or exist: {努力[どりょく]なくして成功[せいこう]はない} 'there is no success without effort'. It is the mirror image of {あっての}.

The noun is usually something abstract and important: support, understanding, effort, love, trust. Adding {は} strengthens the condition.

**Register:** formal and written — speeches, mission statements, editorials. The fixed phrase {涙[なみだ]なくしては語[かた]れない} 'impossible to tell without tears' is common in TV and book blurbs. In conversation, {〜がなければ} is the normal way to say this.

examples.jp: 努力[どりょく]なくして成功[せいこう]はありえない。
examples.en: There can be no success without effort.

examples.jp: 国民[こくみん]の理解[りかい]なくして、増税[ぞうぜい]は進[すす]められない。
examples.en: A tax increase cannot go ahead without the public's understanding.

examples.jp: 皆様[みなさま]のご協力[きょうりょく]なくしては、このプロジェクトは実現[じつげん]できませんでした。
examples.en: This project could never have happened without your cooperation.

examples.jp: 愛[あい]なくして何[なに]の人生[じんせい]か。
examples.en: What is life without love?

points.notes: {〜なしには} (later in this unit) is very similar and slightly less stiff. Both need a negative or 'impossible' meaning in the second half.

quiz.q: 地域[ちいき]住民[じゅうみん]の協力[きょうりょく]＿＿、この祭[まつ]りを続[つづ]けることはできない。
quiz.en: Without the cooperation of local residents, we could not keep this festival going.

quiz.q: 涙[なみだ]＿＿語[かた]れない感動的[かんどうてき]な物語[ものがたり]だ。
quiz.en: It's a moving story that no one can tell without tears.

points.title: 〜ことなしに
points.meaning: without doing X
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ことなしに(は)
points.explanation:
{〜ことなしに} is the verb version of {なくして}: 'without doing X'. It has two typical patterns:

- **Condition:** 'without doing X, Y is impossible' ({努力[どりょく]することなしに成功[せいこう]はない}). Often with {は}.
- **Description:** 'did Y without doing X' ({誰[だれ]にも相談[そうだん]することなしに辞[や]めた}).

**Register:** written and formal — essays, speeches, academic texts. For the second (descriptive) pattern, the slightly less stiff {〜ことなく} is much more common in real writing, and in conversation people just say {〜しないで} or {〜せずに}.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は誰[だれ]にも相談[そうだん]することなしに、会社[かいしゃ]を辞[や]めてしまった。
examples.en: He quit the company without consulting anyone.

examples.jp: 人[ひと]は他人[たにん]と関[かか]わることなしに生[い]きていくことはできない。
examples.en: People cannot live without interacting with others.

examples.jp: 現場[げんば]の声[こえ]を聞[き]くことなしに、正[ただ]しい判断[はんだん]は下[くだ]せない。
examples.en: You can't make the right decision without listening to the people on the ground.

examples.jp: 失敗[しっぱい]を経験[けいけん]することなしには、本当[ほんとう]の成長[せいちょう]はない。
examples.en: Without experiencing failure, there is no real growth.

points.notes: {〜ことなく} = 'without (ever) doing', used heavily in news: {休[やす]むことなく働[はたら]き続[つづ]けた}. {〜ことなしに} leans more towards the 'without X, Y is impossible' pattern.

quiz.q: 努力[どりょく]を続[つづ]ける＿＿、夢[ゆめ]を叶[かな]えることはできない。
quiz.en: You cannot make your dreams come true without continuing to work hard.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]は一度[いちど]も休[やす]む＿＿、三十年間[さんじゅうねんかん]働[はたら]き続[つづ]けた。
quiz.en: She worked for thirty years without taking a single day off.

points.title: 〜なしに／〜なしには
points.meaning: without (permission, notice etc.); without X, (Y is impossible)
points.structure: Noun + (も)なしに / なしで / なしには + negative
points.explanation:
{〜なしに} attaches to a noun and means 'without X'. Typical nouns are things you would normally expect: {断[ことわ]り} (asking first), {許可[きょか]} (permission), {予約[よやく]} (a reservation), {連絡[れんらく]} (contact), {前触[まえぶ]れ} (warning). Adding {も} — {何[なん]の連絡[れんらく]もなしに} — stresses 'without even'.

{〜なしには〜ない} works like {なくしては}: {涙[なみだ]なしには読[よ]めない} 'impossible to read without crying'.

**Register:** neutral to formal, and far more common in real life than {なくして}. You'll see {許可[きょか]なしに} on signs and {断[ことわ]りなしに} in everyday complaints. {なしで} is the most conversational form.

examples.jp: 断[ことわ]りなしに、人[ひと]の部屋[へや]に入[はい]らないでください。
examples.en: Please don't come into someone's room without asking.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は前触[まえぶ]れもなしに、突然[とつぜん]訪[たず]ねてきた。
examples.en: He turned up suddenly without any warning.

examples.jp: 許可[きょか]なしに、この区域[くいき]に立[た]ち入[い]ることは禁止[きんし]されている。
examples.en: Entering this area without permission is prohibited.

examples.jp: この本[ほん]は涙[なみだ]なしには読[よ]めない。
examples.en: You can't read this book without crying.

points.notes: {〜抜[ぬ]きで} is another way to say 'without' when something is deliberately left out: {冗談[じょうだん]抜[ぬ]きで} 'joking aside'.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は何[なん]の連絡[れんらく]も＿＿、会議[かいぎ]を欠席[けっせき]した。
quiz.en: He missed the meeting without any word whatsoever.

quiz.q: 予約[よやく]＿＿入[はい]れる店[みせ]は、この辺[へん]にはほとんどない。
quiz.en: There are hardly any restaurants around here that you can get into without a reservation.

points.title: 〜をおいて
points.meaning: nobody / nothing but X; X is the only one
points.structure: Noun + をおいて(ほかに) + ない / いない
points.explanation:
{〜をおいて} comes from {置[お]く} 'to put aside': 'if you put X aside, there is nobody else'. In other words, X is the one and only choice. It is always followed by a negative: {ほかにいない}, {ほかにない}, {考[かんが]えられない}.

It carries high praise or strong conviction: only this person can do the job, only this place is worth visiting, only now is the right time.

**Register:** formal; used in speeches, recommendations, news commentary and business. It sounds strong and persuasive in speech.

examples.jp: この仕事[しごと]を任[まか]せられるのは、彼[かれ]をおいてほかにいない。
examples.en: There's nobody but him I could entrust this job to.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]の伝統[でんとう]文化[ぶんか]を学[まな]ぶなら、京都[きょうと]をおいてほかにない。
examples.en: If you want to learn about traditional Japanese culture, there's no place like Kyoto.

examples.jp: 今[いま]をおいて、改革[かいかく]のチャンスはない。
examples.en: If we don't reform now, we'll never get another chance.

examples.jp: 次期[じき]社長[しゃちょう]にふさわしい人物[じんぶつ]は、田中[たなか]さんをおいて考[かんが]えられない。
examples.en: I can't think of anyone but Mr Tanaka who is fit to be the next president.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {〜はさておき} 'setting X aside (for now)', which moves on to another topic.

quiz.q: 世界[せかい]記録[きろく]を破[やぶ]れる選手[せんしゅ]は、彼女[かのじょ]＿＿ほかにいない。
quiz.en: There is no athlete but her who could break the world record.

quiz.q: このプロジェクトを成功[せいこう]させられるのは、あなたをおいて＿＿。
quiz.en: You're the only one who can make this project a success.

points.title: 〜いかんで／〜いかんだ
points.meaning: depending on; is determined by
points.structure: Noun (の) + いかんで / いかんによって(は) / いかんだ
points.explanation:
{いかん} (written {如何[いかん]}) is a classical word for 'how, what kind'. {X いかんで Y} means 'Y depends on (how) X (turns out)' — essentially a formal version of {〜次第[しだい]で} or {〜によって}.

- {結果[けっか]いかんで} — depending on the results
- {〜いかんによっては} — depending on X, (something drastic may happen)
- {〜は X いかんだ} — 'it all depends on X'

**Register:** formal and written: business documents, news, official notices, terms and conditions. In speech, {次第[しだい]} is far more natural.

examples.jp: 試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]いかんで、進学先[しんがくさき]が決[き]まる。
examples.en: Which school I go on to depends on my exam results.

examples.jp: 天候[てんこう]いかんでは、大会[たいかい]を延期[えんき]することもあります。
examples.en: Depending on the weather, the tournament may be postponed.

examples.jp: 成功[せいこう]するかどうかは、本人[ほんにん]の努力[どりょく]いかんだ。
examples.en: Whether or not you succeed depends on your own efforts.

examples.jp: 今後[こんご]の交渉[こうしょう]いかんによっては、契約[けいやく]を打[う]ち切[き]る可能性[かのうせい]もある。
examples.en: Depending on how future negotiations go, we may terminate the contract.

points.notes: {いかん} can take {の} before it ({結果[けっか]のいかんで}) — both are fine. Its opposite, 'regardless of', is the next point.

quiz.q: 売[う]り上[あ]げ＿＿、来年度[らいねんど]のボーナスの額[がく]が決[き]まる。
quiz.en: Next year's bonus amount will be decided depending on sales.

quiz.q: 回復[かいふく]の早[はや]さは、患者[かんじゃ]本人[ほんにん]の気力[きりょく]＿＿だ。
quiz.en: How quickly a patient recovers depends on their own willpower.

points.title: 〜いかんによらず／〜いかんを問[と]わず
points.meaning: regardless of; irrespective of
points.structure: Noun + の + いかんによらず / いかんを問[と]わず / いかんにかかわらず
points.explanation:
Adding a negative turns {いかん} into 'regardless of how X is': {理由[りゆう]のいかんによらず} 'regardless of the reason'. Three variants mean the same thing: {いかんによらず}, {いかんを問[と]わず} ('without asking what X is') and {いかんにかかわらず}.

This is the language of rules, refund policies and job ads: no matter the reason, the nationality, the result, the circumstances.

**Register:** very formal and written. You will see it on official notices, contracts and websites ('No refunds for any reason'). In conversation people say {理由[りゆう]はどうであれ} or {〜に関係[かんけい]なく}.

examples.jp: 国籍[こくせき]のいかんを問[と]わず、誰[だれ]でも応募[おうぼ]できる。
examples.en: Anyone can apply, regardless of nationality.

examples.jp: 結果[けっか]のいかんにかかわらず、挑戦[ちょうせん]したことに意味[いみ]がある。
examples.en: Whatever the outcome, there is meaning in having tried.

examples.jp: 事情[じじょう]のいかんを問[と]わず、無断[むだん]欠席[けっせき]は認[みと]めない。
examples.en: Unexcused absences will not be accepted, whatever the circumstances.

examples.jp: 理由[りゆう]のいかんによらず、一度[いちど]納[おさ]めた料金[りょうきん]はお返[かえ]しできません。
examples.en: Once paid, fees cannot be refunded for any reason.

points.notes: The everyday equivalents are {〜を問[と]わず} and {〜にかかわらず} without {いかん}: {年齢[ねんれい]を問[と]わず} 'regardless of age'.

quiz.q: 理由[りゆう]の＿＿、遅刻[ちこく]した者[もの]は試験[しけん]を受[う]けられません。
quiz.en: Whatever the reason, anyone who arrives late will not be allowed to sit the exam.

quiz.q: 年齢[ねんれい]・性別[せいべつ]の＿＿を問[と]わず、どなたでも参加[さんか]できます。
quiz.en: Anyone may participate, regardless of age or gender.

points.title: 〜とあれば
points.meaning: if it's (for) X, then (I'd do anything / it can't be helped)
points.structure: Noun / Verb (plain) + とあれば
points.explanation:
{〜とあれば} means 'if the situation is X'. It is used when X is a special reason that justifies doing something you normally wouldn't — or that leaves no choice: 'If it's for my children, I'll put up with anything', 'If it's the boss's order, I have to obey'.

Very common with {〜のためとあれば} and {必要[ひつよう]とあれば} 'if necessary'. The second half usually shows willingness or acceptance.

**Register:** somewhat formal, but used in speech too, especially {必要[ひつよう]とあれば} in business. Its sibling {とあって} (Unit 6) states a real reason rather than a hypothetical one.

examples.jp: 必要[ひつよう]とあれば、いつでもご説明[せつめい]に伺[うかが]います。
examples.en: If necessary, I can come and explain at any time.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どものためとあれば、親[おや]はどんな苦労[くろう]もいとわない。
examples.en: When it's for their children, parents will put up with any hardship.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]の命令[めいれい]とあれば、従[したが]わないわけにはいかない。
examples.en: If it's an order from the president, I have no choice but to obey.

examples.jp: 大好[だいす]きな歌手[かしゅ]が来[く]るとあれば、何時間[なんじかん]でも並[なら]ぶつもりだ。
examples.en: If my favourite singer is coming, I'm prepared to queue for hours.

points.notes: Not for neutral conditions like {✕雨[あめ]とあれば中止[ちゅうし]する}; use {雨[あめ]なら} or {雨[あめ]の場合[ばあい]は}. {とあれば} implies the condition is a strong motivation.

quiz.q: 愛[あい]する家族[かぞく]のため＿＿、どんな仕事[しごと]でもする。
quiz.en: If it's for my beloved family, I'll do any kind of work.

quiz.q: お客様[きゃくさま]のご要望[ようぼう]＿＿、できる限[かぎ]り対応[たいおう]いたします。
quiz.en: If it is what our customers request, we will accommodate it as far as we can.

units.title: Not even, let alone, no need to
units.summary: Emphatic and concessive patterns: 'even' ({すら}), 'not even one' ({たりとも}), 'let alone' ({はおろか}), 'whether/even if' ({であれ}, {といえども}), 'if not X, at least Y' ({ないまでも}) and 'there's no need' ({までもない}).

points.title: 〜すら
points.meaning: even (emphasising an extreme example)
points.structure: Noun (+ particle) + すら / Noun + ですら
points.explanation:
{すら} means 'even' and works almost exactly like {さえ}: it picks out an extreme example to imply that everything else is true too. 'There's not even time to eat lunch' implies there's no time for anything at all.

It is most often used in negative or surprising statements. After a noun that is the subject, {ですら} is common: {専門家[せんもんか]ですら} 'even experts'.

**Register:** {すら} is more written and a little more dramatic than {さえ}. You'll see it constantly in essays, news and novels; in conversation {さえ} or {も} is more usual, though {すら} is not unusual in serious speech.

examples.jp: 忙[いそが]しくて、昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べる時間[じかん]すらない。
examples.en: I'm so busy I don't even have time to eat lunch.

examples.jp: そんな簡単[かんたん]なことは、子[こ]どもですら知[し]っている。
examples.en: Even a child knows something that simple.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は自分[じぶん]の名前[なまえ]すら漢字[かんじ]で書[か]けなかった。
examples.en: He couldn't even write his own name in kanji.

examples.jp: 専門家[せんもんか]ですら予測[よそく]できなかった事態[じたい]が起[お]きた。
examples.en: Something happened that not even the experts could have predicted.

points.notes: Unlike {さえ}, {すら} is not used in the conditional pattern {〜さえ〜ば} 'if only': {時間[じかん]さえあれば} (not {✕時間[じかん]すらあれば}).

quiz.q: 疲[つか]れ果[は]てて、立[た]ち上[あ]がる力[ちから]＿＿残[のこ]っていなかった。
quiz.en: I was so exhausted I didn't even have the strength left to stand up.

quiz.q: この問題[もんだい]は、大学[だいがく]の先生[せんせい]で＿＿解[と]けなかった。
quiz.en: Not even the university professors could solve this problem.

points.title: 〜たりとも
points.meaning: not even one (yen / day / second ...)
points.structure: 一[いち]／一[ひと] + counter (一円[いちえん]・一日[いちにち]・一瞬[いっしゅん]) + たりとも + negative
points.explanation:
{〜たりとも} attaches to the smallest possible quantity — {一円[いちえん]}, {一日[いちにち]}, {一瞬[いっしゅん]}, {一人[ひとり]}, {一歩[いっぽ]} — and is followed by a negative: 'not even a single X'. It expresses a strong, uncompromising attitude: no exceptions, no waste, no letting your guard down.

The second half is often a prohibition or obligation: {〜てはいけない}, {〜わけにはいかない}, {〜な}, {〜ない}.

**Register:** formal and emphatic — speeches, sports, news, military or dramatic contexts. In everyday speech you'd say {一円[いちえん]も}, but {一瞬[いっしゅん]たりとも} is heard in pep talks and commentary.

examples.jp: 一円[いちえん]たりとも無駄[むだ]にはできない。
examples.en: We can't afford to waste even a single yen.

examples.jp: 一瞬[いっしゅん]たりとも気[き]を抜[ぬ]いてはいけない。
examples.en: You mustn't let your guard down for even a moment.

examples.jp: 試験[しけん]まであと一週間[いっしゅうかん]だ。一日[いちにち]たりとも休[やす]むわけにはいかない。
examples.en: There's only a week left until the exam. I can't take even one day off.

examples.jp: 敵[てき]を一歩[いっぽ]たりとも中[なか]に入[い]れるな。
examples.en: Don't let the enemy take a single step inside.

points.notes: It only works with 'one' plus a counter (or a small fixed amount). {✕百円[ひゃくえん]たりとも} sounds strange.

quiz.q: 税金[ぜいきん]は国民[こくみん]のお金[かね]だ。一円[いちえん]＿＿無駄[むだ]に使[つか]ってはならない。
quiz.en: Tax is the people's money. Not a single yen must be wasted.

quiz.q: 手術中[しゅじゅつちゅう]は一瞬[いっしゅん]たりとも気[き]を＿＿。
quiz.en: During surgery you can't relax your concentration for even a moment.

points.title: 〜はおろか
points.meaning: let alone; not to mention
points.structure: Noun + はおろか、 ... も／さえ／すら + (usually negative)
points.explanation:
{X はおろか Y も} means 'not only X, but even Y' — where X is the obvious, bigger thing and Y is the smaller, more basic one. For example, 'He can't even read hiragana, let alone kanji.' Note the Japanese order: the big thing comes first ({漢字[かんじ]はおろか}), the basic thing second ({ひらがなも読[よ]めない}).

{おろか} means 'foolish': it is foolish even to mention X. The tone is usually negative, surprised or critical.

**Register:** written and formal, but you will hear it in serious conversation. The neutral equivalents are {〜どころか} and {〜はもちろん}.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は漢字[かんじ]はおろか、ひらがなも読[よ]めない。
examples.en: He can't even read hiragana, let alone kanji.

examples.jp: 忙[いそが]しすぎて、旅行[りょこう]はおろか、週末[しゅうまつ]に休[やす]むこともできない。
examples.en: I'm so busy I can't even take weekends off, never mind go on a trip.

examples.jp: 大[おお]けがをして、走[はし]ることはおろか、歩[ある]くことさえできない。
examples.en: With this serious injury, I can't even walk, let alone run.

examples.jp: その村[むら]には、病院[びょういん]はおろか、コンビニ一軒[いっけん]すらない。
examples.en: That village doesn't even have a convenience store, let alone a hospital.

points.notes: Can't be used with commands, requests or intentions in the second half. For positive 'not only... but also', use {〜はもとより} or {〜はもちろん}.

quiz.q: 私[わたし]は海外[かいがい]旅行[りょこう]＿＿、国内[こくない]旅行[りょこう]もほとんどしたことがない。
quiz.en: I've hardly ever travelled even within the country, let alone abroad.

quiz.q: 足[あし]を骨折[こっせつ]して、走[はし]ることはおろか、立[た]つこと＿＿できない。
quiz.en: I broke my leg, so I can't even stand, let alone run.

points.title: 〜であれ／〜であれ〜であれ
points.meaning: whatever / whoever X is; whether X or Y
points.structure: Noun / question word + であれ / Noun₁ + であれ + Noun₂ + であれ
points.explanation:
{であれ} is the command form of the classical copula {である}, used to mean 'be it X'. It has three common patterns:

- **Question word + {であれ}:** {何[なん]であれ} 'whatever it is', {誰[だれ]であれ} 'whoever it is'.
- **{たとえ} + Noun + {であれ}:** 'even if it is X'.
- **X {であれ} Y {であれ}:** 'whether X or Y' — the conclusion applies equally to both.

The second half states a general rule or a firm judgement.

**Register:** formal and written, though {何[なん]であれ} and {理由[りゆう]はどうであれ} turn up in serious conversation. The colloquial version is {〜でも〜でも}.

examples.jp: 理由[りゆう]が何[なん]であれ、暴力[ぼうりょく]は許[ゆる]されない。
examples.en: Whatever the reason, violence is unacceptable.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもであれ大人[おとな]であれ、ルールは守[まも]らなければならない。
examples.en: Whether you're a child or an adult, you have to follow the rules.

examples.jp: たとえ社長[しゃちょう]であれ、間違[まちが]いは間違[まちが]いだ。
examples.en: Even if it's the president, a mistake is a mistake.

examples.jp: 晴[は]れであれ雨[あめ]であれ、試合[しあい]は予定[よてい]どおり行[おこな]われる。
examples.en: Rain or shine, the match will be held as scheduled.

points.notes: A related form is {〜であろうと(〜であろうと)}, with the same meaning. Don't confuse {であれ} with {であれば} 'if it is'.

quiz.q: 相手[あいて]が誰[だれ]＿＿、言[い]うべきことははっきり言[い]う。
quiz.en: Whoever I'm dealing with, I say clearly what needs to be said.

quiz.q: 小説[しょうせつ]であれ詩[し]＿＿、良[よ]い作品[さくひん]には心[こころ]を動[うご]かす力[ちから]がある。
quiz.en: Whether it's a novel or a poem, a good work has the power to move people.

points.title: 〜といえども
points.meaning: even though; even (if one is) X
points.structure: Noun / plain form + といえども
points.explanation:
{〜といえども} means 'even though it is X / even an X', with the strong implication that X is someone or something you'd expect to be an exception — but isn't. 'Even a professional chef makes mistakes', 'Even the prime minister will be judged if he breaks the law'.

It often follows a noun of status or an extreme case, and sometimes comes with {いかに} or {たとえ}. The second half is a general truth or a firm judgement.

**Register:** formal and written — editorials, speeches, legal and business contexts. In conversation you'd use {〜でも} or {〜とはいっても}.

examples.jp: プロの料理人[りょうりにん]といえども、失敗[しっぱい]することはある。
examples.en: Even professional chefs sometimes make mistakes.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもといえども、一人[ひとり]の人間[にんげん]として尊重[そんちょう]すべきだ。
examples.en: Even a child should be respected as an individual.

examples.jp: 一国[いっこく]の首相[しゅしょう]といえども、法[ほう]を犯[おか]せば裁[さば]かれる。
examples.en: Even a nation's prime minister will be tried if he breaks the law.

examples.jp: 景気[けいき]が回復[かいふく]しつつあるといえども、楽観[らっかん]はできない。
examples.en: Although the economy is recovering, we cannot be optimistic.

points.notes: {といえども} is stronger and more formal than {とはいえ} (Unit 10). {〜といえども} also appears in {一瞬[いっしゅん]といえども} 'not even for a moment', similar to {たりとも}.

quiz.q: 冬[ふゆ]＿＿、沖縄[おきなわ]は日中[にっちゅう]なら半袖[はんそで]で過[す]ごせる日[ひ]もある。
quiz.en: Even in winter, there are days in Okinawa when you can wear short sleeves during the day.

quiz.q: いかに優秀[ゆうしゅう]な医者[いしゃ]＿＿、すべての患者[かんじゃ]を救[すく]えるわけではない。
quiz.en: No matter how excellent a doctor is, they cannot save every patient.

points.title: 〜ないまでも
points.meaning: even if not (as much as) X, at least Y
points.structure: Verb ない-form + までも
points.explanation:
{X ないまでも Y} means 'it may not reach X, but at least Y'. X is a high level, Y is a more modest level that the speaker hopes for, requests or acknowledges. The second half often has {せめて}, {少[すこ]しは}, {〜たい}, {〜べきだ} or {〜てほしい}.

The most frequent forms are {〜とは言[い]わないまでも} 'I won't go so far as to say X, but...' and {〜ないまでも、せめて〜}.

**Register:** neutral to formal, used in both writing and conversation. Practical and fairly common.

examples.jp: 毎日[まいにち]とは言[い]わないまでも、週[しゅう]に一度[いちど]は運動[うんどう]したほうがいい。
examples.en: Maybe not every day, but you should exercise at least once a week.

examples.jp: 優勝[ゆうしょう]はできないまでも、せめて決勝[けっしょう]には進[すす]みたい。
examples.en: Even if we can't win, I'd like us to at least reach the final.

examples.jp: 完璧[かんぺき]でないまでも、ある程度[ていど]は話[はな]せるようになった。
examples.en: Though not perfectly, I've become able to speak to some extent.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の行為[こうい]は、犯罪[はんざい]とは言[い]えないまでも、かなり問題[もんだい]がある。
examples.en: What he did may not be a crime, but it's very problematic.

points.notes: Compare {〜までもない} (next point), which means 'there's no need to'. One extra {も} and a negative in a different place changes the meaning completely.

quiz.q: 満点[まんてん]は取[と]れない＿＿、せめて八十点[はちじゅってん]は取[と]りたい。
quiz.en: Even if I can't get full marks, I want to get at least eighty.

quiz.q: プロ並[な]みとは言[い]わ＿＿、もう少[すこ]し上手[じょうず]に歌[うた]えるようになりたい。
quiz.en: I don't mean professional level, but I'd like to be able to sing a bit better.

points.title: 〜までもない
points.meaning: there's no need to (go as far as); it goes without saying
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + までもない / までもなく
points.explanation:
{〜までもない} means 'it isn't necessary to go as far as doing X' because the matter is simple or obvious. You don't need to call a repairman, you don't need to check again, you don't need to explain.

The most common expression by far is {言[い]うまでもない} / {言[い]うまでもなく} 'needless to say' — extremely frequent in essays, speeches and business writing.

**Register:** neutral to formal. {言[い]うまでもなく} is something you'll use yourself in presentations and reports; other verbs are fine in conversation too.

examples.jp: 言[い]うまでもなく、健康[けんこう]は何[なに]よりも大切[たいせつ]だ。
examples.en: Needless to say, health is more important than anything.

examples.jp: こんな簡単[かんたん]な修理[しゅうり]なら、業者[ぎょうしゃ]を呼[よ]ぶまでもない。
examples.en: For a repair this simple, there's no need to call in a professional.

examples.jp: 結果[けっか]は、改[あらた]めて確認[かくにん]するまでもなく明[あき]らかだった。
examples.en: The result was obvious without even having to check again.

examples.jp: わざわざ説明[せつめい]するまでもないことだが、締[し]め切[き]りは厳守[げんしゅ]してください。
examples.en: It hardly needs explaining, but please strictly observe the deadline.

points.notes: Similar to {〜ことはない} 'there's no need to', but {までもない} adds 'it's too obvious/simple to bother'.

quiz.q: 近[ちか]いから、タクシーに乗[の]る＿＿。歩[ある]いて行[い]こう。
quiz.en: It's close, so there's no need to take a taxi. Let's walk.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]が優秀[ゆうしゅう]なのは、言[い]う＿＿。
quiz.en: It goes without saying that he is excellent.

points.title: 〜までだ／〜までのことだ
points.meaning: (1) I'll just (do X), that's all; (2) I merely did X
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + までだ / Verb (た-form) + までだ
points.explanation:
{まで} here means 'only as far as'. Two uses:

**1. Dictionary form:** 'If plan A fails, I'll simply do B — no big deal.' It shows calm determination: {電車[でんしゃ]がないなら、歩[ある]いて帰[かえ]るまでだ} 'If there are no trains, I'll just walk home.'

**2. ta-form:** 'I merely did X (and nothing more)' — used to downplay one's actions or to say there was no hidden intention: {当然[とうぜん]のことをしたまでです} 'I only did what anyone would.'

{〜までのことだ} is a slightly more emphatic version.

**Register:** fairly formal but used in speech, especially use 2 when someone thanks you. Use 1 sounds resolute, a bit like a hero in a drama.

examples.jp: 電車[でんしゃ]がないなら、歩[ある]いて帰[かえ]るまでだ。
examples.en: If there are no trains, I'll just walk home.

examples.jp: 気[き]にしないでください。当然[とうぜん]のことをしたまでです。
examples.en: Please don't mention it. I only did what anyone would have done.

examples.jp: 反対[はんたい]されても、自分[じぶん]の信[しん]じる道[みち]を進[すす]むまでのことだ。
examples.en: Even if people oppose me, I'll simply follow the path I believe in.

examples.jp: 私[わたし]は事実[じじつ]を述[の]べたまでで、誰[だれ]かを批判[ひはん]するつもりはない。
examples.en: I was merely stating the facts; I have no intention of criticising anyone.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {〜までもない} 'no need to'. {までだ} = 'I'll just do it'; {までもない} = 'no need to do it'.

quiz.q: 今年[ことし]の試験[しけん]に落[お]ちたら、また来年[らいねん]受[う]ける＿＿。
quiz.en: If I fail this year's exam, I'll simply take it again next year.

quiz.q: お礼[れい]なんていりません。私[わたし]は自分[じぶん]の仕事[しごと]をした＿＿です。
quiz.en: There's no need to thank me. I was just doing my job.

units.title: Special circumstances and status
units.summary: Patterns that point to a special situation or rank and what follows from it: {とあって}, {ともなると}, {ならでは}, {たる}, {にあって}, {にして}, and the size-emphasiser {からある}.

points.title: 〜とあって
points.meaning: because it is (a special occasion), (naturally)
points.structure: Noun / plain form + とあって
points.explanation:
{X とあって Y} reports a real situation X that is special or unusual, and a result Y that follows naturally from it. 'Because it was a public holiday, the tourist spots were packed.' 'Because a famous singer was coming, people queued from the morning.'

The speaker observes the result from the outside, so Y is a description of what happened — not the speaker's will, a request or a command.

**Register:** a staple of news reports and written description ({〜とあって、多[おお]くの人[ひと]でにぎわった} is practically a TV news template). Not common in casual speech, where people say {〜だから}.

examples.jp: 連休[れんきゅう]とあって、観光地[かんこうち]はどこも人[ひと]でいっぱいだった。
examples.en: Since it was a long weekend, tourist spots everywhere were packed.

examples.jp: 初[はじ]めての海外[かいがい]旅行[りょこう]とあって、娘[むすめ]は前[まえ]の晩[ばん]からそわそわしていた。
examples.en: It was her first trip abroad, so my daughter was restless from the night before.

examples.jp: 人気[にんき]歌手[かしゅ]が来[く]るとあって、会場[かいじょう]には朝[あさ]から長[なが]い列[れつ]ができた。
examples.en: Because a popular singer was coming, a long queue formed at the venue from the morning.

examples.jp: 年末[ねんまつ]のセールとあって、デパートは買[か]い物客[ものきゃく]でにぎわっている。
examples.en: With the year-end sales on, the department stores are bustling with shoppers.

points.notes: {とあって} = real, special circumstance → natural result. {とあれば} (Unit 4) = hypothetical 'if it's for X, I'd do anything'.

quiz.q: 久[ひさ]しぶりの晴天[せいてん]の週末[しゅうまつ]＿＿、公園[こうえん]は家族[かぞく]連[づ]れでにぎわった。
quiz.en: As it was the first sunny weekend in a while, the park was bustling with families.

quiz.q: 有名[ゆうめい]な監督[かんとく]の最新作[さいしんさく]＿＿、公開[こうかい]初日[しょにち]から映画館[えいがかん]は満員[まんいん]だった。
quiz.en: Since it was a famous director's latest film, cinemas were full from the opening day.

points.title: 〜ともなると／〜ともなれば
points.meaning: when it comes to (a higher level / special stage), naturally ...
points.structure: Noun / Verb (dictionary form) + ともなると / ともなれば
points.explanation:
{〜ともなると} means 'once you reach the level / stage of X, things are (naturally) different'. X is usually a higher position, age, season or scale: {大学生[だいがくせい]ともなると}, {社長[しゃちょう]ともなれば}, {十二月[じゅうにがつ]ともなると}, {一流[いちりゅう]ホテルともなると}.

The second half describes what is normal or expected at that level, often with {〜なければならない}, {〜だろう} or a description of a change.

**Register:** neutral-formal; quite common in both speech and writing. Very similar to {〜となると}, with {も} adding emphasis that X is a step up.

examples.jp: 十二月[じゅうにがつ]ともなると、街[まち]はクリスマスの飾[かざ]りでいっぱいになる。
examples.en: Once December comes, the streets fill with Christmas decorations.

examples.jp: 大学生[だいがくせい]ともなると、自分[じぶん]のことは自分[じぶん]で決[き]めなければならない。
examples.en: Once you're a university student, you have to make your own decisions.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]ともなれば、休日[きゅうじつ]もゆっくり休[やす]めないだろう。
examples.en: When you're the company president, you probably can't relax even on your days off.

examples.jp: 一流[いちりゅう]のホテルともなると、サービスの質[しつ]がまるで違[ちが]う。
examples.en: When it comes to a top-class hotel, the quality of service is completely different.

points.notes: Unlike {とあって}, which refers to one specific event, {ともなると} talks about what is generally true at a certain level.

quiz.q: 子[こ]どもも中学生[ちゅうがくせい]＿＿、親[おや]と出[で]かけたがらなくなる。
quiz.en: Once children reach middle school, they stop wanting to go out with their parents.

quiz.q: プロの選手[せんしゅ]とも＿＿、毎日[まいにち]の練習量[れんしゅうりょう]は相当[そうとう]なものだ。
quiz.en: When it comes to professional athletes, the amount they train each day is considerable.

points.title: 〜ならでは
points.meaning: unique to; only X could (do / have) this
points.structure: Noun + ならではの + Noun / Noun + ならではだ
points.explanation:
{X ならではの Y} means 'Y that only X has / only X can offer'. It praises something as characteristic of, and special to, a particular place, person or thing: {京都[きょうと]ならではの風情[ふぜい]} 'atmosphere you can only find in Kyoto', {手作[てづく]りならではの温[あたた]かみ} 'the warmth only handmade things have'.

It's almost always positive and evaluative.

**Register:** this is one of the most useful N1 points in daily life. It is everywhere in advertising, travel guides, menus, TV food shows and reviews. You'll hear it and can use it in conversation too.

examples.jp: 京都[きょうと]ならではの風情[ふぜい]を楽[たの]しんでください。
examples.en: Please enjoy the atmosphere that only Kyoto can offer.

examples.jp: 手作[てづく]りならではの温[あたた]かみがある。
examples.en: It has a warmth that only comes with handmade things.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもならではの自由[じゆう]な発想[はっそう]に驚[おどろ]かされた。
examples.en: I was amazed by the free-spirited ideas that only a child could come up with.

examples.jp: このような繊細[せんさい]な表現[ひょうげん]は、ベテラン俳優[はいゆう]ならではだ。
examples.en: Such subtle expression is something only a veteran actor could achieve.

points.notes: An older pattern, {X ならでは Y ない} 'only X could do Y', also exists ({彼[かれ]ならではできない仕事[しごと]}), but {ならではの} is by far the most common form today.

quiz.q: 雪[ゆき]の中[なか]の露天[ろてん]風呂[ぶろ]は、冬[ふゆ]の北海道[ほっかいどう]＿＿体験[たいけん]だ。
quiz.en: An outdoor hot spring in the snow is an experience unique to Hokkaido in winter.

quiz.q: この細[こま]かい手仕事[てしごと]は、熟練[じゅくれん]した職人[しょくにん]＿＿だ。
quiz.en: Only a skilled craftsman could do such fine handiwork.

points.title: 〜たる
points.meaning: as one who is (X), (one should); worthy of the name X
points.structure: Noun (role / status) + たる + 者[もの]／もの／Noun
points.explanation:
{たる} is a classical form of {である} used before a noun. {X たる者[もの]} means 'anyone who is an X (worthy of the name)'. It sets up a moral standard: because you hold this role, you must behave accordingly.

The nouns are roles with responsibility: {教師[きょうし]}, {医者[いしゃ]}, {政治家[せいじか]}, {首相[しゅしょう]}, {社会人[しゃかいじん]}, {リーダー}. The second half is usually {〜べきだ}, {〜なければならない} or a criticism ({〜とは情[なさ]けない}).

**Register:** formal, slightly old-fashioned and preachy. Common in editorials, speeches and in older people's lectures. {社会人[しゃかいじん]たるもの} is a well-known phrase in company training.

examples.jp: 社会人[しゃかいじん]たるもの、時間[じかん]を守[まも]るのは当然[とうぜん]だ。
examples.en: As a working adult, it's only natural to be punctual.

examples.jp: 教師[きょうし]たる者[もの]、生徒[せいと]の手本[てほん]とならなければならない。
examples.en: Anyone who is a teacher must set an example for their students.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]には、リーダーたる資格[しかく]がない。
examples.en: He doesn't have what it takes to be a true leader.

examples.jp: 一国[いっこく]の首相[しゅしょう]たる者[もの]が、軽率[けいそつ]な発言[はつげん]をするべきではない。
examples.en: A person who is a nation's prime minister should not make careless remarks.

points.notes: The opposite moral judgement — behaviour unworthy of a role — uses {〜にあるまじき} (Unit 13).

quiz.q: 医者[いしゃ]＿＿者[もの]、患者[かんじゃ]の命[いのち]を第一[だいいち]に考[かんが]えるべきだ。
quiz.en: Anyone who is a doctor should put patients' lives first.

quiz.q: 社会人[しゃかいじん]たる＿＿、言葉[ことば]遣[づか]いには気[き]をつけなければならない。
quiz.en: As a working adult, you must be careful about how you speak.

points.title: 〜にあって
points.meaning: in (a situation / position / era)
points.structure: Noun + にあって(は／も)
points.explanation:
{〜にあって} is a formal way of saying 'in (this situation)', literally 'being in X'. X is a special circumstance, position or era: {厳[きび]しい状況[じょうきょう]にあって}, {部長[ぶちょう]という立場[たちば]にあって}, {現代[げんだい]にあって}.

- {〜にあっては} — 'in X, (as you'd expect)...'
- {〜にあっても} — 'even in X, (surprisingly)...'

**Register:** formal and written — news analysis, speeches, business reports, essays. You'll rarely hear it in casual speech, where {〜の中[なか]で} or {〜で} is used.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は病床[びょうしょう]にあっても、最後[さいご]まで執筆[しっぴつ]を続[つづ]けた。
examples.en: Even from his sickbed, he kept on writing until the end.

examples.jp: 部長[ぶちょう]という立場[たちば]にあって、そのような発言[はつげん]は許[ゆる]されない。
examples.en: In your position as department head, such remarks are unacceptable.

examples.jp: 厳[きび]しい経済[けいざい]状況[じょうきょう]にあって、同社[どうしゃ]は過去[かこ]最高[さいこう]の利益[りえき]を上[あ]げた。
examples.en: Despite the harsh economic conditions, the company posted record profits.

examples.jp: 情報[じょうほう]があふれる現代[げんだい]にあって、何[なに]を信[しん]じるかが問[と]われている。
examples.en: In this modern age flooded with information, we are being challenged to decide what to believe.

points.notes: Compare {〜において}, which is the more neutral formal 'in/at' ({会議[かいぎ]において}). {〜にあって} emphasises that the situation is special.

quiz.q: 少子[しょうし]高齢化[こうれいか]が進[すす]む日本[にほん]＿＿、外国人[がいこくじん]労働者[ろうどうしゃ]の役割[やくわり]はますます大[おお]きくなっている。
quiz.en: In Japan, with its ageing population and falling birth rate, the role of foreign workers is becoming ever more important.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]は逆境[ぎゃっきょう]＿＿も、決[けっ]して希望[きぼう]を失[うしな]わなかった。
quiz.en: Even in adversity, she never lost hope.

points.title: 〜にして
points.meaning: (1) only at the level of X; (2) at (the age / time of) X; (3) both X and Y
points.structure: Noun + にして
points.explanation:
{〜にして} is a versatile formal particle. Its main uses:

**1. Level reached:** {X にして初[はじ]めて} 'only someone at level X could' — {名医[めいい]にして初[はじ]めて可能[かのう]な手術[しゅじゅつ]}.

**2. Point in time / age:** 'at (only) X' or 'after as long as X', often with {ようやく} or a note of surprise: {三十歳[さんじゅっさい]にして社長[しゃちょう]になった}, {結婚[けっこん]十年目[じゅうねんめ]にして}.

**3. Instantly:** {一瞬[いっしゅん]にして}, {一夜[いちや]にして} 'in an instant, overnight'.

**4. 'Both X and Y':** {医者[いしゃ]にして作家[さっか]} 'a doctor and also a writer'.

**Register:** written and formal; news, biographies, literature. Use 3 is common everywhere.

examples.jp: 一瞬[いっしゅん]にして、すべてが炎[ほのお]に包[つつ]まれた。
examples.en: In an instant, everything was engulfed in flames.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は三十歳[さんじゅっさい]にして、会社[かいしゃ]の社長[しゃちょう]になった。
examples.en: He became company president at just thirty.

examples.jp: 結婚[けっこん]十年目[じゅうねんめ]にして、ようやく子[こ]どもを授[さず]かった。
examples.en: After ten years of marriage, they were finally blessed with a child.

examples.jp: この難[むずか]しい手術[しゅじゅつ]は、彼[かれ]ほどの名医[めいい]にして初[はじ]めて可能[かのう]だ。
examples.en: Only a doctor as skilled as he is could perform this difficult operation.

points.notes: Learn the set phrases first: {一瞬[いっしゅん]にして}, {一夜[いちや]にして}, {〜にして初[はじ]めて}. Not to be confused with {〜にしては} 'for (a beginner etc.), surprisingly'.

quiz.q: 五度目[ごどめ]の挑戦[ちょうせん]＿＿、ついに司法[しほう]試験[しけん]に合格[ごうかく]した。
quiz.en: On his fifth attempt, he finally passed the bar exam.

quiz.q: 地震[じしん]で、町[まち]は一瞬[いっしゅん]＿＿瓦礫[がれき]の山[やま]と化[か]した。
quiz.en: In the earthquake, the town was reduced to rubble in an instant.

points.title: 〜からある／〜からの
points.meaning: as much as; no less than; a good (X) or more
points.structure: Number + counter + からある (size, weight, length) / からする (price) / からの (number of people/things) + Noun

examples.jp: 二十[にじゅっ]キロからある道[みち]を歩[ある]いて帰[かえ]った。
examples.en: I walked all the way home — a good twenty kilometres.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は百[ひゃく]キロからある荷物[にもつ]を一人[ひとり]で運[はこ]んだ。
examples.en: He carried a load weighing no less than a hundred kilos by himself.

examples.jp: その事故[じこ]で、千人[せんにん]からの乗客[じょうきゃく]が足止[あしど]めされた。
examples.en: As many as a thousand passengers were stranded because of the accident.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]がつけていたのは、一千万円[いっせんまんえん]からする指輪[ゆびわ]だった。
examples.en: The ring she was wearing cost no less than ten million yen.

points.notes: Only with large, impressive numbers — {✕一[いち]キロからある} sounds wrong.

quiz.q: その男[おとこ]は、二[に]メートル＿＿大[おお]きな魚[さかな]を釣[つ]り上[あ]げた。
quiz.en: The man landed a huge fish no less than two metres long.

quiz.q: 会場[かいじょう]の前[まえ]には、五千人[ごせんにん]＿＿ファンが詰[つ]めかけた。
quiz.en: As many as five thousand fans crowded in front of the venue.

units.title: Covered in, full of, -ish
units.summary: Suffixes that attach to nouns to describe appearance, quantity and attitude: {ずくめ}, {まみれ}, {めく}, {ぐるみ}, {じみる}, and the belittling {ごとき}.

points.title: 〜ずくめ
points.meaning: nothing but; entirely X; X from head to toe
points.structure: Noun + ずくめ (だ／の + Noun)
points.explanation:
{〜ずくめ} means something consists entirely of X. It is used with a limited set of nouns:

- **Colours, especially black:** {黒[くろ]ずくめの男[おとこ]} 'a man dressed all in black'
- **Good things:** {いいことずくめ}, {おめでたいことずくめ}, {ごちそうずくめ}
- **Rules or restrictions:** {規則[きそく]ずくめ} 'rules everywhere'

Unlike {まみれ} and {だらけ}, it is often positive.

**Register:** neutral; it's used in conversation, TV and writing. {いいことずくめ} is a common everyday phrase, and {黒[くろ]ずくめ} appears often in crime reports and mystery stories.

examples.jp: 今年[ことし]はいいことずくめの一年[いちねん]だった。
examples.en: This year was nothing but good things.

examples.jp: 黒[くろ]ずくめの男[おとこ]が、店[みせ]の前[まえ]に立[た]っていた。
examples.en: A man dressed all in black was standing in front of the shop.

examples.jp: この学校[がっこう]は規則[きそく]ずくめで、息[いき]が詰[つ]まりそうだ。
examples.en: This school has rules for everything; it's suffocating.

examples.jp: 結婚[けっこん]に昇進[しょうしん]と、今年[ことし]はおめでたいことずくめだ。
examples.en: Marriage, then a promotion — this year has been one celebration after another.

points.notes: Don't overextend it: {✕間違[まちが]いずくめ} is wrong; use {間違[まちが]いだらけ}.

quiz.q: 昇進[しょうしん]、結婚[けっこん]、新居[しんきょ]の購入[こうにゅう]と、今年[ことし]は良[よ]いこと＿＿だった。
quiz.en: A promotion, marriage and a new home — this year has been full of good things.

quiz.q: 犯人[はんにん]は黒[くろ]＿＿の服装[ふくそう]をしていたという。
quiz.en: The culprit was reportedly dressed entirely in black.

points.title: 〜まみれ
points.meaning: covered in; smeared with (something dirty or unpleasant)
points.structure: Noun + まみれ (になる／だ／の + Noun)
points.explanation:
{〜まみれ} means the whole surface is covered in something, usually dirty, sticky or liquid: {泥[どろ]まみれ} (mud), {汗[あせ]まみれ} (sweat), {血[ち]まみれ} (blood), {ほこりまみれ} (dust), {油[あぶら]まみれ} (oil). It can also be used figuratively, for things that 'stick' to you and drag you down: {借金[しゃっきん]まみれ} 'up to one's ears in debt'.

**Register:** neutral and quite common in conversation, news and fiction. It's a vivid, physical word.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもたちは泥[どろ]まみれになって遊[あそ]んでいた。
examples.en: The kids were playing and getting covered in mud.

examples.jp: 真夏[まなつ]の工事[こうじ]現場[げんば]で、作業員[さぎょういん]たちは汗[あせ]まみれで働[はたら]いていた。
examples.en: At the construction site in midsummer, the workers were drenched in sweat.

examples.jp: 事故[じこ]現場[げんば]には、血[ち]まみれの男性[だんせい]が倒[たお]れていた。
examples.en: A man covered in blood was lying at the scene of the accident.

examples.jp: 事業[じぎょう]に失敗[しっぱい]した彼[かれ]は、借金[しゃっきん]まみれの生活[せいかつ]を送[おく]っている。
examples.en: After his business failed, he's been living up to his ears in debt.

points.notes: {〜だらけ} means 'full of / lots of' and works with things that aren't spread over a surface ({間違[まちが]いだらけ}, {傷[きず]だらけ}). {まみれ} is specifically about being coated. {ほこりだらけ} and {ほこりまみれ} are both fine.

quiz.q: 雨[あめ]の中[なか]で試合[しあい]をした選手[せんしゅ]たちは、泥[どろ]＿＿になった。
quiz.en: The players who played in the rain ended up covered in mud.

quiz.q: 長年[ながねん]使[つか]われていない倉庫[そうこ]の荷物[にもつ]は、ほこり＿＿だった。
quiz.en: The goods in the warehouse, unused for years, were covered in dust.

points.title: 〜めく／〜めいた
points.meaning: to show signs of; to seem like; -ish
points.structure: Noun + めく / めいて / めいた + Noun
points.explanation:
{〜めく} turns a noun into a verb meaning 'to take on the feel of X'. Two typical uses:

- **Seasons:** {春[はる]めく}, {秋[あき]めく} — 'to start feeling like spring/autumn'. Very common in weather reports and letters.
- **Manner:** {冗談[じょうだん]めいた} (joking), {皮肉[ひにく]めいた} (sarcastic), {謎[なぞ]めいた} (mysterious), {言[い]い訳[わけ]めいた} (sounding like an excuse), {秘密[ひみつ]めいた} (secretive).

Before a noun it usually appears as {めいた}.

**Register:** somewhat written, but common in seasonal greetings, weather, literature and descriptions. It only works with a fixed set of nouns.

examples.jp: 三月[さんがつ]に入[はい]り、日差[ひざ]しもだいぶ春[はる]めいてきた。
examples.en: Now that it's March, the sunshine is starting to feel quite spring-like.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は冗談[じょうだん]めいた口調[くちょう]で、本音[ほんね]を漏[も]らした。
examples.en: In a half-joking tone, he let slip what he really thought.

examples.jp: 謎[なぞ]めいた微笑[ほほえ]みを浮[う]かべて、彼女[かのじょ]は去[さ]っていった。
examples.en: With an enigmatic smile, she walked away.

examples.jp: 言[い]い訳[わけ]めいたことは言[い]いたくないが、事情[じじょう]を説明[せつめい]させてほしい。
examples.en: I don't want to make excuses, but please let me explain the circumstances.
