points.notes: {めく} is fairly neutral; {じみる} (later in this unit) is critical. Compare {皮肉[ひにく]めいた} (a little sarcastic) and {子[こ]どもじみた} (childish, disapproving).

quiz.q: 木々[きぎ]が色[いろ]づき始[はじ]め、山[やま]もすっかり秋[あき]＿＿きた。
quiz.en: The trees have begun to change colour, and the mountains are really starting to look autumnal.

quiz.q: 上司[じょうし]の皮肉[ひにく]＿＿言[い]い方[かた]が気[き]になった。
quiz.en: My boss's somewhat sarcastic way of putting it bothered me.

points.title: 〜ぐるみ
points.meaning: the whole (family / town / company); including all of
points.structure: Noun + ぐるみ (で／の + Noun)
points.explanation:
{〜ぐるみ} comes from {くるむ} 'to wrap up'. It means 'X as a whole, everybody in X included': {家族[かぞく]ぐるみの付[つ]き合[あ]い} 'a friendship between whole families', {町[まち]ぐるみで} 'the entire town together', {会社[かいしゃ]ぐるみの不正[ふせい]} 'company-wide wrongdoing'.

The nouns are groups: {家族[かぞく]}, {町[まち]}, {地域[ちいき]}, {学校[がっこう]}, {会社[かいしゃ]}, {組織[そしき]}. The idiom {身[み]ぐるみ剥[は]がされる} means 'to be robbed of everything (down to one's clothes)'.

**Register:** neutral; common in news ({組織[そしき]ぐるみの犯行[はんこう]} 'an organised crime involving the whole group') and in everyday talk about neighbours.

examples.jp: うちとお隣[となり]は、家族[かぞく]ぐるみの付[つ]き合[あ]いをしている。
examples.en: Our family and the family next door are friends with each other.

examples.jp: 町[まち]ぐるみで、ごみの削減[さくげん]に取[と]り組[く]んでいる。
examples.en: The whole town is working together to reduce rubbish.

examples.jp: 今回[こんかい]の不正[ふせい]は、会社[かいしゃ]ぐるみで行[おこな]われていた疑[うたが]いがある。
examples.en: It is suspected that this fraud was carried out company-wide.

examples.jp: 旅行先[りょこうさき]で強盗[ごうとう]に遭[あ]い、身[み]ぐるみ剥[は]がされた。
examples.en: I was robbed while travelling and lost everything I had on me.

points.notes: {〜ぐるみ} is different from {ぬいぐるみ} (stuffed toy) and {着[き]ぐるみ} (mascot costume), though they share the same 'wrapping' origin.

quiz.q: 子[こ]どもの安全[あんぜん]を守[まも]るため、地域[ちいき]＿＿でパトロールを行[おこな]っている。
quiz.en: To keep children safe, the whole community carries out patrols.

quiz.q: 警察[けいさつ]は、組織[そしき]＿＿の犯行[はんこう]と見[み]て捜査[そうさ]を進[すす]めている。
quiz.en: The police are investigating it as a crime involving the whole organisation.

points.title: 〜じみる／〜じみた
points.meaning: to smack of; to seem like (in a bad way); childish / theatrical etc.
points.structure: Noun + じみる / じみて / じみた + Noun
points.explanation:
{〜じみる} means 'to take on an (unwelcome) quality of X'. It is critical: the thing isn't really X, but it looks or feels like X, and the speaker disapproves.

Common combinations: {子[こ]どもじみた} (childish), {年寄[としよ]りじみた} (fogeyish), {芝居[しばい]じみた} (theatrical, fake), {脅迫[きょうはく]じみた} (threatening), {所帯[しょたい]じみた} (looking worn down by domestic life).

**Register:** neutral; used in both conversation and writing. {子[こ]どもじみた} is the one you'll hear most.

examples.jp: いい大人[おとな]が、そんな子[こ]どもじみたことを言[い]うな。
examples.en: You're a grown adult — don't say such childish things.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の謝罪[しゃざい]は、どこか芝居[しばい]じみていた。
examples.en: His apology seemed somehow staged.

examples.jp: まだ二十代[にじゅうだい]なのに、年寄[としよ]りじみた服[ふく]ばかり着[き]ている。
examples.en: He's still in his twenties, but he only wears clothes that make him look like an old man.

examples.jp: 取引先[とりひきさき]から、脅迫[きょうはく]じみたメールが届[とど]いた。
examples.en: We received an almost threatening email from a client.

points.notes: Comparison: {〜っぽい} (casual, neutral), {〜めく} (neutral, signs of), {〜じみる} (critical), {〜らしい} (typical of a real X).

quiz.q: 三十歳[さんじゅっさい]にもなって、そんな子[こ]ども＿＿わがままを言[い]うものではない。
quiz.en: At thirty, you shouldn't be making such childish demands.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]の大[おお]げさな涙[なみだ]は、芝居[しばい]＿＿いて信用[しんよう]できない。
quiz.en: His exaggerated tears seem theatrical, and I can't believe them.

points.title: 〜ごとき (the likes of)
points.meaning: the likes of; a mere (humble or contemptuous)
points.structure: Noun + ごとき (が／に／で) / Noun + ごとき + Noun
points.explanation:
{ごとき} originally means 'like, similar to' (see {ごとし} in Unit 14). After a person or thing, it has a strong evaluative meaning: 'the likes of X, a mere X'.

- **Humble (about yourself):** {私[わたし]ごとき} 'someone like me' — modest, very polite.
- **Contemptuous (about others):** {お前[まえ]ごとき} 'the likes of you', {新人[しんじん]ごときが} 'a mere newcomer'.
- **Dismissive (about things):** {風邪[かぜ]ごときで休[やす]めない} 'can't take time off for a mere cold'.

**Register:** literary and dramatic. The humble use appears in formal speech; the contemptuous use is common in manga, anime and dramas (villains love it). Be very careful using it about others in real life — it's insulting.

examples.jp: 私[わたし]ごとき者[もの]に、このような大役[たいやく]が務[つと]まるでしょうか。
examples.en: Could someone like me really fulfil such an important role?

examples.jp: 風邪[かぜ]ごときで会社[かいしゃ]を休[やす]むわけにはいかない。
examples.en: I can't take a day off work for a mere cold.

examples.jp: お前[まえ]ごときに負[ま]けるはずがない。
examples.en: There's no way I'd lose to the likes of you.

examples.jp: 新人[しんじん]ごときが、社長[しゃちょう]に意見[いけん]するなんて生意気[なまいき]だ。
examples.en: It's cheeky for a mere newcomer to voice opinions to the president.

points.notes: A softer, more common equivalent is {〜なんか／〜なんて} ({私[わたし]なんか}). {ごとき} sounds far more dramatic.

quiz.q: 私[わたし]＿＿の意見[いけん]が参考[さんこう]になるかどうか分[わ]かりませんが…。
quiz.en: I'm not sure the opinion of someone like me will be of any use, but...

quiz.q: こんな小[ちい]さなけが＿＿で、試合[しあい]を休[やす]むわけにはいかない。
quiz.en: I can't miss the match over such a minor injury.

units.title: Bad endings, bad habits
units.summary: Patterns for things going wrong: deplorable outcomes ({始末[しまつ]だ}), bad tendencies ({きらいがある}), things never done ({ずじまい}), 'that's the end of it' ({ばそれまでだ}), regret ({ものを}), points of no return ({が最後[さいご]}) and 'this is going too far' ({にもほどがある}).

points.title: 〜始末[しまつ]だ
points.meaning: (and) ended up (doing something deplorable); it's come to the point where
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + 始末[しまつ]だ
points.explanation:
{始末[しまつ]} can mean 'outcome' or 'mess'. {〜始末[しまつ]だ} comes at the end of a story about a chain of bad behaviour or worsening problems, introducing the final, worst result: 'He kept drinking, and in the end he got arrested.'

The speaker is critical or exasperated. Typical lead-ins are {ついには}, {とうとう}, {挙[あ]げ句[く]の果[は]てに}, or a list of earlier bad things.

**Register:** neutral to slightly formal; you'll hear it in complaints and gossip as well as read it in essays. Related phrase: {この始末[しまつ]だ} 'and look at this mess'.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は酒[さけ]に酔[よ]って暴[あば]れ、警察[けいさつ]を呼[よ]ばれる始末[しまつ]だった。
examples.en: He got drunk and violent, and it came to the point where the police were called.

examples.jp: 部下[ぶか]はミスを認[みと]めないどころか、私[わたし]のせいにする始末[しまつ]だ。
examples.en: Far from admitting his mistake, my subordinate has even started blaming me.

examples.jp: 何度[なんど]注意[ちゅうい]しても遅刻[ちこく]を繰[く]り返[かえ]し、この前[まえ]は無断[むだん]で休[やす]む始末[しまつ]だ。
examples.en: No matter how often I warn him he keeps coming in late, and the other day he even took the day off without telling anyone.

examples.jp: 息子[むすこ]は遊[あそ]んでばかりで、ついには大学[だいがく]を退学[たいがく]させられる始末[しまつ]だ。
examples.en: My son did nothing but play, and in the end he got expelled from university.

points.notes: Only for bad results. For a neutral outcome, use {〜ことになった} or {結局[けっきょく]〜}.

quiz.q: 夫[おっと]は毎晩[まいばん]飲[の]み歩[ある]き、とうとう体[からだ]を壊[こわ]して入院[にゅういん]する＿＿。
quiz.en: My husband went out drinking every night, and in the end he ruined his health and ended up in hospital.
choices: に越[こ]したことはない

quiz.q: あの子[こ]は宿題[しゅくだい]をしないばかりか、先生[せんせい]に嘘[うそ]をつく＿＿だ。
quiz.en: Not only does that child not do his homework, he's even started lying to his teacher.

points.title: 〜きらいがある
points.meaning: to have a (bad) tendency to
points.structure: Verb (dictionary / ない-form) + きらいがある / Noun + の + きらいがある
points.explanation:
{きらい} here is written {嫌[きら]い} but it doesn't mean 'dislike'; it means a regrettable inclination. {〜きらいがある} says someone or something tends to do X, and the speaker sees it as a flaw: tends to take on too much, tends to jump to conclusions, tends to put problems off.

It's usually used to criticise others or groups in a measured, analytical way, rarely about oneself.

**Register:** formal and written — essays, editorials, performance reviews, critiques. In conversation, {〜がちだ} or {〜傾向[けいこう]がある} are more common.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は何[なん]でも一人[ひとり]で抱[かか]え込[こ]むきらいがある。
examples.en: He has a tendency to take everything on by himself.

examples.jp: 最近[さいきん]の若者[わかもの]は、すぐに結論[けつろん]を求[もと]めるきらいがある。
examples.en: Young people these days tend to want answers right away.

examples.jp: この国[くに]の政治家[せいじか]は、問題[もんだい]を先送[さきおく]りにするきらいがある。
examples.en: This country's politicians have a habit of putting off problems.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]の文章[ぶんしょう]は、やや説明[せつめい]過剰[かじょう]のきらいがある。
examples.en: Her writing tends to be somewhat over-explained.

points.notes: Not for positive tendencies: {✕彼[かれ]は親切[しんせつ]にするきらいがある}. Note that it is about nature or habit, not a one-off action.

quiz.q: 部長[ぶちょう]は人[ひと]の話[はなし]を最後[さいご]まで聞[き]かずに判断[はんだん]する＿＿。
quiz.en: The department head has a tendency to make decisions without hearing people out.

quiz.q: 日本人[にほんじん]は自分[じぶん]の意見[いけん]をはっきり言[い]わない＿＿があると言[い]われる。
quiz.en: It is said that Japanese people tend not to state their opinions clearly.

points.title: 〜ずじまい
points.meaning: ended up never doing (to one's regret)
points.structure: Verb ない-stem + ずじまい (だ／で) — する → せずじまい
points.explanation:
{〜ずじまい} combines classical negative {ず} with {しまい} 'the end': 'it ended without X ever happening'. You intended or wanted to do something, the chance passed, and now it's too late. There's a feeling of regret or disappointment.

Often with {結局[けっきょく]}, {とうとう}, {一度[いちど]も}. Remember the irregular forms: {する} → {せずじまい}, {来[く]る} → {来[こ]ずじまい}.

**Register:** neutral; genuinely common in conversation and writing. One of the most practical points in this unit.

examples.jp: 忙[いそが]しくて、結局[けっきょく]その映画[えいが]は見[み]ずじまいだった。
examples.en: I was so busy that in the end I never got to see that film.

examples.jp: 旅行[りょこう]中[ちゅう]ずっと雨[あめ]で、富士山[ふじさん]は見[み]えずじまいだった。
examples.en: It rained the whole trip, so we never got to see Mount Fuji.

examples.jp: 祖父[そふ]には、とうとう本当[ほんとう]の気持[きも]ちを言[い]えずじまいだった。
examples.en: In the end, I never managed to tell my grandfather how I really felt.

examples.jp: せっかく買[か]った参考書[さんこうしょ]も、一度[いちど]も開[ひら]かずじまいで試験[しけん]の日[ひ]を迎[むか]えた。
examples.en: The exam day came, and I'd never once opened the study guide I'd bought.

points.notes: It describes a past period that is over. For an ongoing situation, use {まだ〜ていない}.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]の連絡先[れんらくさき]を聞[き]こうと思[おも]ったが、結局[けっきょく]聞[き]け＿＿だった。
quiz.en: I meant to ask for her contact details, but in the end I never managed to.

quiz.q: 京都[きょうと]に三年[さんねん]住[す]んでいたのに、金閣寺[きんかくじ]には一度[いちど]も＿＿じまいだった。
quiz.en: Even though I lived in Kyoto for three years, I never once went to Kinkaku-ji.

points.title: 〜ばそれまでだ
points.meaning: if X, that's the end of it; it's all for nothing if X
points.structure: Verb ば-form + それまでだ / Verb たら + それまでだ
points.explanation:
{〜ばそれまでだ} means 'if X happens, everything stops there — all previous effort is wasted'. However good, expensive or carefully prepared something is, one simple failure (forgetting, dying, not using it) makes it meaningless.

A second, very common use: {〜と言[い]ってしまえばそれまでだが} 'you could just say X and leave it at that, but...' — used to reject an easy explanation and dig deeper.

**Register:** neutral; common in conversation, essays and opinion pieces.

examples.jp: どんなに高[たか]い薬[くすり]も、飲[の]み忘[わす]れればそれまでだ。
examples.en: However expensive the medicine, it's useless if you forget to take it.

examples.jp: いくら貯金[ちょきん]しても、死[し]んでしまえばそれまでだ。
examples.en: No matter how much you save, it's all over when you die.

examples.jp: せっかくのチャンスも、生[い]かさなければそれまでだ。
examples.en: Even a great opportunity is worthless if you don't make use of it.

examples.jp: 「才能[さいのう]がない」と言[い]ってしまえばそれまでだが、努力[どりょく]が足[た]りなかったのも事実[じじつ]だ。
examples.en: You could just say 'I had no talent' and leave it at that, but the truth is I also didn't work hard enough.

points.notes: Often paired with {せっかく}, {どんなに}, {いくら} in the first half to emphasise wasted effort.

quiz.q: どんなに準備[じゅんび]をしても、当日[とうじつ]寝坊[ねぼう]すれば＿＿。
quiz.en: However well you prepare, it's all for nothing if you oversleep on the day.

quiz.q: 運[うん]が悪[わる]かったと言[い]ってしまえば＿＿が、原因[げんいん]はほかにもあったはずだ。
quiz.en: You could just put it down to bad luck, but there must have been other causes too.

points.title: 〜ものを
points.meaning: if only ...; (X would have happened), but
points.structure: Verb / Adjective (plain form, often with ば／たら) + ものを
points.explanation:
{〜ものを} expresses regret, complaint or reproach about something that could have been but wasn't. 'If you'd asked me, I would have helped — (but you didn't)'. The first half is usually a hypothetical with {〜ば／〜たら}, and {ものを} implies a 'but' — the actual result was disappointing.

It can end the sentence (leaving the regret hanging) or continue into what actually happened.

**Register:** somewhat literary and slightly old-fashioned, but still used in speech for complaints: {言[い]ってくれれば手伝[てつだ]ったものを}. Similar to {〜のに}, but stronger in reproach.

examples.jp: 一言[ひとこと]相談[そうだん]してくれれば手伝[てつだ]ったものを。
examples.en: If only you'd said something, I would have helped.

examples.jp: 黙[だま]っていればいいものを、余計[よけい]なことを言[い]って怒[おこ]らせてしまった。
examples.en: He should have just kept quiet, but he said something unnecessary and made her angry.

examples.jp: 早[はや]く病院[びょういん]に行[い]けば治[なお]ったものを、彼[かれ]は我慢[がまん]し続[つづ]けた。
examples.en: It would have healed if he'd gone to the hospital early, but he kept putting up with it.

examples.jp: 素直[すなお]に謝[あやま]れば許[ゆる]してもらえたものを、彼[かれ]は最後[さいご]まで言[い]い訳[わけ]をした。
examples.en: He would have been forgiven if he'd simply apologised, but he made excuses to the end.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {〜ものの} 'although' or {〜ものか} 'as if I would!'.

quiz.q: 言[い]ってくれれば、駅[えき]まで迎[むか]えに行[い]った＿＿。
quiz.en: If you'd told me, I would have come to pick you up at the station.

quiz.q: 最初[さいしょ]から本当[ほんとう]のことを話[はな]せばいい＿＿、嘘[うそ]をついたせいで問題[もんだい]が大[おお]きくなった。
quiz.en: She should have just told the truth from the start, but because she lied, the problem got bigger.

points.title: 〜が最後[さいご]／〜たら最後[さいご]
points.meaning: once X happens, (there's no going back / something bad always follows)
points.structure: Verb (た-form) + が最後[さいご] / たら最後[さいご]
points.explanation:
{〜が最後[さいご]} means 'once X happens, that's it' — the moment X occurs, an unstoppable or irreversible (usually bad) situation follows. Once you tell her a secret, the whole office knows; once he starts gaming, he won't stop for hours; once trust is lost, it's hard to get back.

It often describes habits or general truths, so the second half is commonly in the present tense.

**Register:** {が最後[さいご]} is more written; {たら最後[さいご]} is more conversational and genuinely used in speech.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]はゲームを始[はじ]めたら最後[さいご]、何時間[なんじかん]でもやめない。
examples.en: Once he starts playing a game, he won't stop for hours.

examples.jp: このソファは、一度[いちど]座[すわ]ったが最後[さいご]、なかなか立[た]ち上[あ]がれない。
examples.en: Once you sit on this sofa, it's really hard to get up again.

examples.jp: あの人[ひと]に話[はな]したが最後[さいご]、翌日[よくじつ]には会社中[かいしゃじゅう]に広[ひろ]まってしまう。
examples.en: Once you tell that person something, the whole company knows about it by the next day.

examples.jp: 信用[しんよう]は一度[いちど]失[うしな]ったが最後[さいご]、取[と]り戻[もど]すのは難[むずか]しい。
examples.en: Once you lose people's trust, it's hard to win it back.

points.notes: {一度[いちど]} often appears in the first half. Unlike {〜たとたん}, the focus is on the irreversible consequence rather than timing.

quiz.q: 父[ちち]は一度[いちど]怒[おこ]り出[だ]した＿＿、誰[だれ]にも止[と]められない。
quiz.en: Once my father starts getting angry, nobody can stop him.

quiz.q: この森[もり]は、一度[いちど]迷[まよ]い込[こ]んだ＿＿、二度[にど]と出[で]られないと言[い]われている。
quiz.en: They say that once you get lost in this forest, you can never get out again.

points.title: 〜にもほどがある
points.meaning: there's a limit to (how X); this is too X
points.structure: Noun / な-adj stem / Verb・い-adj (plain) + にもほどがある
points.explanation:
{ほど} means 'limit, degree'. {〜にもほどがある} literally says 'even X has its limits' — i.e. 'this is going way too far'. It's a strong criticism of someone being excessively rude, careless, reckless or silly.

Common combinations: {冗談[じょうだん]にもほどがある} 'that's not funny anymore', {非常識[ひじょうしき]にもほどがある}, {無責任[むせきにん]にもほどがある}, {わがままにもほどがある}, {失礼[しつれい]にもほどがある}.

**Register:** conversational and emotional — you'll hear it from irritated people in real life, in dramas and on social media. It's strong, so use it with care.

examples.jp: 冗談[じょうだん]にもほどがある。
examples.en: A joke's a joke, but this is going too far.

examples.jp: 三時間[さんじかん]も遅刻[ちこく]するなんて、非常識[ひじょうしき]にもほどがある。
examples.en: Being three hours late is outrageously inconsiderate.

examples.jp: 一人[ひとり]で冬山[ふゆやま]に登[のぼ]るなんて、無謀[むぼう]にもほどがある。
examples.en: Climbing a mountain alone in winter is way too reckless.

examples.jp: 人[ひと]の好意[こうい]をそこまで疑[うたが]うとは、ひねくれているにもほどがある。
examples.en: Being that suspicious of other people's kindness is just too twisted.

points.notes: Often preceded by {〜なんて} or {〜とは}, which introduce the shocking behaviour.

quiz.q: 約束[やくそく]を三回[さんかい]も破[やぶ]るなんて、いい加減[かげん]＿＿。
quiz.en: Breaking your promise three times — there's a limit to how unreliable you can be.

quiz.q: いくら疲[つか]れているからといって、会議中[かいぎちゅう]に寝[ね]るなんて、失礼[しつれい]にも＿＿がある。
quiz.en: I know you're tired, but falling asleep during a meeting is far too rude.

units.title: Inevitable, unavoidable, deserved
units.summary: Patterns of necessity and judgement: 'will inevitably' ({ずにはおかない}), 'can't get away without' ({ずにはすまない}), 'be forced to' ({を余儀[よぎ]なくされる}), grudging possibility, 'easy to imagine', 'worthy of', and 'deserves to'.

points.title: 〜ずにはおかない
points.meaning: will inevitably (cause); can't fail to; will definitely (do)
points.structure: Verb ない-stem + ずにはおかない (する → せずにはおかない)
points.explanation:
{〜ずにはおかない} literally means 'will not leave things without doing X'. Two uses:

**1. Inevitable effect (most common):** the subject is a thing — a film, a remark, a policy — and it will inevitably cause a reaction. Often with causative verbs: {感動[かんどう]させずにはおかない} 'can't fail to move people', {批判[ひはん]を招[まね]かずにはおかない} 'is bound to draw criticism'.

**2. Strong determination:** a person declares they will definitely do something: {犯人[はんにん]を捕[つか]まえずにはおかない} 'I will catch the culprit, no matter what'.

**Register:** formal and written — reviews, editorials, news commentary. The variant {〜ないではおかない} means the same.

examples.jp: この映画[えいが]は、見[み]る人[ひと]を感動[かんどう]させずにはおかない。
examples.en: This film cannot fail to move whoever watches it.

examples.jp: 今度[こんど]こそ、犯人[はんにん]を捕[つか]まえずにはおかない。
examples.en: This time, I'm going to catch the culprit, no matter what.

examples.jp: 新[あたら]しい税制[ぜいせい]は、国民[こくみん]の生活[せいかつ]に影響[えいきょう]を与[あた]えずにはおかない。
examples.en: The new tax system is bound to affect people's lives.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の無責任[むせきにん]な発言[はつげん]は、世間[せけん]の批判[ひはん]を招[まね]かずにはおかないだろう。
examples.en: His irresponsible remarks will inevitably draw public criticism.

points.notes: Compare {〜ずにはいられない} 'I can't help doing' (the speaker's own uncontrollable urge). {ずにはおかない} is about an unstoppable effect on others, or an iron will.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]の歌声[うたごえ]は、聞[き]く人[ひと]の心[こころ]を動[うご]かさ＿＿。
quiz.en: Her singing voice cannot fail to move the hearts of those who hear it.

quiz.q: この事件[じけん]は、社会[しゃかい]に大[おお]きな衝撃[しょうげき]を与[あた]え＿＿だろう。
quiz.en: This incident is bound to send a great shock through society.

points.title: 〜ずにはすまない／〜ないではすまない
points.meaning: won't get away without doing; will have to (by social obligation)
points.structure: Verb ない-stem + ずにはすまない / Verb ない-form + ではすまない (する → せずにはすまない)
points.explanation:
{すむ} means 'to be settled, to be over'. {〜ずにはすまない} means 'the matter won't be settled unless X is done' — i.e. given the situation, social norms or common sense demand that you do X. You broke something, so you'll have to pay; you caused trouble, so you'll have to apologise.

The obligation comes from the situation, not from the speaker's personal desire.

**Register:** formal; used in writing and in serious conversation. The variant {〜ないではすまない} is slightly more conversational. A related form is {〜ではすまない} 'won't end at X' ({謝[あやま]るだけではすまない} 'an apology alone won't be enough').

examples.jp: 大切[たいせつ]な書類[しょるい]をなくしたのだから、部長[ぶちょう]に謝[あやま]らずにはすまない。
examples.en: I lost important documents, so I'll have to apologise to the department head.

examples.jp: 友達[ともだち]の車[くるま]を傷[きず]つけてしまった。弁償[べんしょう]せずにはすまないだろう。
examples.en: I damaged my friend's car. I'll probably have to pay for it.

examples.jp: 嘘[うそ]がばれた以上[いじょう]、本当[ほんとう]のことを話[はな]さないではすまない。
examples.en: Now that the lie has come out, I'll have no choice but to tell the truth.

examples.jp: これほどの事故[じこ]を起[お]こした以上[いじょう]、会社[かいしゃ]の責任[せきにん]が問[と]われずにはすまないだろう。
examples.en: Having caused an accident this serious, the company is bound to be held responsible.

points.notes: {ずにはおかない} = something will inevitably cause an effect (or iron will); {ずにはすまない} = the situation obliges you to do something.

quiz.q: 約束[やくそく]を破[やぶ]って迷惑[めいわく]をかけたのだから、直接[ちょくせつ]会[あ]って謝[あやま]ら＿＿。
quiz.en: I broke my promise and caused trouble, so I'll have to meet them in person and apologise.

quiz.q: 会社[かいしゃ]のお金[かね]を使[つか]い込[こ]んだのだから、処分[しょぶん]を受[う]けないでは＿＿。
quiz.en: Since he embezzled company money, he won't get away without being disciplined.

points.title: 〜を余儀[よぎ]なくされる
points.meaning: to be forced to; to have no choice but to
points.structure: Noun (action) + を余儀[よぎ]なくされる / Noun + を余儀[よぎ]なくさせる (to force)
points.explanation:
{余儀[よぎ]ない} means 'unavoidable, no other option'. {X を余儀[よぎ]なくされる} means 'to be forced (by circumstances) into X' — typically something unwelcome like cancellation, withdrawal, retirement, closure or evacuation. X is a noun, usually a Sino-Japanese action noun: {中止[ちゅうし]}, {欠航[けっこう]}, {撤退[てったい]}, {閉鎖[へいさ]}, {引退[いんたい]}, {避難[ひなん]}.

The active form {〜を余儀[よぎ]なくさせる} puts the cause as the subject: 'the typhoon forced the cancellation'.

**Register:** very formal, and **extremely common in news**. You'll hear it on NHK every week. In conversation, you'd say {〜しなければならなくなった}.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]はけがのため、引退[いんたい]を余儀[よぎ]なくされた。
examples.en: He was forced to retire because of injury.

examples.jp: 台風[たいふう]の影響[えいきょう]で、多[おお]くの便[びん]が欠航[けっこう]を余儀[よぎ]なくされた。
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, many flights had to be cancelled.

examples.jp: 業績[ぎょうせき]の悪化[あっか]により、同社[どうしゃ]は工場[こうじょう]の閉鎖[へいさ]を余儀[よぎ]なくされた。
examples.en: Due to deteriorating results, the company was forced to close the factory.

examples.jp: 突然[とつぜん]の豪雨[ごうう]が、大会[たいかい]の中止[ちゅうし]を余儀[よぎ]なくさせた。
examples.en: The sudden downpour forced the tournament to be called off.

points.notes: The forced action is generally negative and caused by external circumstances (weather, the economy, injury), not by a person's order.

quiz.q: 大雪[おおゆき]のため、新幹線[しんかんせん]は運転[うんてん]見合[みあ]わせ＿＿。
quiz.en: Due to heavy snow, the Shinkansen was forced to suspend operations.
choices: を禁[きん]じ得[え]なかった
を皮切[かわき]りにした
を余儀[よぎ]なくされた
をものともしなかった

quiz.q: 資金[しきん]不足[ぶそく]により、研究[けんきゅう]チームは計画[けいかく]の変更[へんこう]を余儀[よぎ]なく＿＿。
quiz.en: Due to a lack of funds, the research team was forced to change its plans.

points.title: 〜ないものでもない
points.meaning: it's not impossible that; might (just) (if conditions are right)
points.structure: Verb ない-form + ものでもない / ものでもありません
points.explanation:
A double negative: {〜ないものでもない} means 'it's not the case that X can't/won't happen'. It expresses a reluctant, hedged possibility: 'I might be willing, depending on the conditions', 'we might just make it if we hurry'.

It often comes with a condition: {条件[じょうけん]次第[しだい]では}, {急[いそ]げば}, {〜があれば}. The speaker is cautious and not committing.

**Register:** somewhat formal and a little roundabout; used in negotiations and in careful speech or writing. The everyday equivalent is {〜ないこともない}, which is much more common.

examples.jp: 条件[じょうけん]次第[しだい]では、引[ひ]き受[う]けないものでもない。
examples.en: Depending on the terms, I might be willing to take it on.

examples.jp: 急[いそ]げば、最終[さいしゅう]電車[でんしゃ]に間[ま]に合[あ]わないものでもない。
examples.en: If we hurry, we might just make the last train.

examples.jp: 誠意[せいい]ある謝罪[しゃざい]があれば、許[ゆる]さないものでもない。
examples.en: If I get a sincere apology, I might be willing to forgive him.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の気持[きも]ちも分[わ]からないものでもないが、やはり規則[きそく]は規則[きそく]だ。
examples.en: It's not that I don't understand how he feels, but rules are rules.

points.notes: Learn {〜ないこともない} as the spoken version: {行[い]かないこともないけど…} 'I might go, I suppose...'.

quiz.q: 三日[みっか]あれば、できない＿＿が、確約[かくやく]はできない。
quiz.en: If I had three days, it might not be impossible, but I can't promise anything.

quiz.q: 君[きみ]がそこまで言[い]うなら、手伝[てつだ]ってあげない＿＿。
quiz.en: If you insist that much, I suppose I might help you.

points.title: 〜にかたくない
points.meaning: it is not hard to (imagine / understand)
points.structure: Noun (想像[そうぞう]・理解[りかい]) + にかたくない / Verb (察[さっ]する) + にかたくない
points.explanation:
{かたい} here is {難[かた]い} 'difficult' (an old, written word). {〜にかたくない} means 'it is not difficult to X' — and in practice the X is almost always imagining or understanding: {想像[そうぞう]にかたくない} 'easy to imagine', {察[さっ]するにかたくない} 'easy to guess (someone's feelings)', {理解[りかい]にかたくない}.

It's used when the speaker infers something (often someone's suffering, or a likely future consequence) from the situation.

**Register:** formal and written — editorials, essays, news commentary. {想像[そうぞう]にかたくない} is by far the most common form; learn it as a set phrase.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]がどれほど緊張[きんちょう]していたかは、想像[そうぞう]にかたくない。
examples.en: It's easy to imagine how nervous she must have been.

examples.jp: 突然[とつぜん]家族[かぞく]を失[うしな]った彼[かれ]の悲[かな]しみは、想像[そうぞう]にかたくない。
examples.en: It's not hard to imagine his grief at suddenly losing his family.

examples.jp: 一人[ひとり]で三人[さんにん]の子[こ]どもを育[そだ]てる苦労[くろう]は、察[さっ]するにかたくない。
examples.en: One can easily imagine the hardship of raising three children alone.

examples.jp: このまま値上[ねあ]げが続[つづ]けば、消費者[しょうひしゃ]の反発[はんぱつ]が強[つよ]まることは想像[そうぞう]にかたくない。
examples.en: If prices keep rising like this, it's easy to imagine consumer backlash growing.

points.notes: Don't use it with everyday verbs: {✕このパンは食[た]べるにかたくない}. It's reserved for imagining and understanding.

quiz.q: 被災者[ひさいしゃ]の不安[ふあん]は、想像[そうぞう]＿＿。
quiz.en: It's not hard to imagine the anxiety of the disaster victims.
choices: を余儀[よぎ]なくされる

quiz.q: 初[はじ]めて一人[ひとり]で海外[かいがい]に出[で]た娘[むすめ]の心細[こころぼそ]さは、察[さっ]する＿＿かたくない。
quiz.en: It's easy to imagine how lonely my daughter felt going abroad alone for the first time.

points.title: 〜に足[た]る／〜に足[た]りない
points.meaning: worthy of; enough to justify / not worth
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) / Noun + に足[た]る (+ Noun) / に足[た]りない
points.explanation:
{足[た]る} is the classical form of {足[た]りる} 'to be enough'. {X に足[た]る Y} means 'Y that is sufficient for X / worthy of X': {信頼[しんらい]するに足[た]る人物[じんぶつ]} 'a person worthy of trust', {証明[しょうめい]するに足[た]る証拠[しょうこ]} 'evidence sufficient to prove it'.

The negative {〜に足[た]りない} means 'not worth X'. The fixed phrase {取[と]るに足[た]りない} 'trivial, not worth bothering about' is very common.

**Register:** formal and written — reports, legal language, essays. {取[と]るに足[た]りない} also appears in everyday conversation.

examples.jp: そんなことは取[と]るに足[た]りない問題[もんだい]だ。
examples.en: That's a trivial problem.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は信頼[しんらい]するに足[た]る人物[じんぶつ]だ。
examples.en: He is a man who can be trusted.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の主張[しゅちょう]を裏付[うらづ]けるに足[た]る証拠[しょうこ]は見[み]つからなかった。
examples.en: No evidence sufficient to back up his claim was found.

examples.jp: 満足[まんぞく]に足[た]る結果[けっか]とは言[い]えないが、一定[いってい]の成果[せいか]はあった。
examples.en: It can't be called a satisfying result, but there was some progress.

points.notes: Compare {〜に値[あたい]する} 'worth (doing)': {一読[いちどく]に値[あたい]する} 'worth reading'. {〜に足[た]る} focuses on sufficiency, {〜に値[あたい]する} on value.

quiz.q: その報告書[ほうこくしょ]には、信用[しんよう]する＿＿データが一[ひと]つもなかった。
quiz.en: There was not a single piece of data in that report worthy of trust.

quiz.q: 小[ちい]さなミスなど、気[き]にするに＿＿。
quiz.en: Small mistakes aren't worth worrying about.

points.title: 〜でなくてなんだろう
points.meaning: if this isn't X, what is?; this is surely X
points.structure: Noun + でなくてなんだろう(か) / でなくてなんであろう(か)
points.explanation:
A rhetorical question: 'If this is not X, then what is it?' — meaning 'this is X, without doubt'. The writer describes something striking, then labels it with strong emotion: love, fate, courage, a miracle, abuse, injustice.

The noun is usually abstract and weighty: {愛[あい]}, {運命[うんめい]}, {奇跡[きせき]}, {勇気[ゆうき]}, {悲劇[ひげき]}, {差別[さべつ]}.

**Register:** literary and rhetorical — essays, speeches, novels, impassioned editorials. You will almost never hear it in conversation; if you used it at a party, people would think you were giving a speech.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]が命[いのち]をかけて子[こ]どもを救[すく]ったのは、勇気[ゆうき]でなくてなんだろう。
examples.en: He risked his life to save a child — if that isn't courage, what is?

examples.jp: 何十年[なんじゅうねん]も離[はな]れていた二人[ふたり]が偶然[ぐうぜん]再会[さいかい]した。これが運命[うんめい]でなくてなんだろうか。
examples.en: Two people separated for decades met again by chance. If that isn't fate, what is?

examples.jp: 自分[じぶん]の夢[ゆめ]を捨[す]ててまで家族[かぞく]を支[ささ]えた母[はは]の生[い]き方[かた]は、愛[あい]でなくてなんだろう。
examples.en: My mother gave up her own dreams to support our family. What could that be but love?

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもに食[た]べ物[もの]を与[あた]えず放置[ほうち]するのは、虐待[ぎゃくたい]でなくてなんであろう。
examples.en: Leaving a child without food — if that isn't abuse, what is?

points.notes: {なんであろう} is even more literary than {なんだろう}. The pattern always expresses the writer's strong conviction.

quiz.q: 一度[いちど]も会[あ]ったことのない人々[ひとびと]のために一生[いっしょう]を捧[ささ]げる。これが愛[あい]＿＿。
quiz.en: Devoting your whole life to people you've never met — if that isn't love, what is?

quiz.q: 十年[じゅうねん]もの研究[けんきゅう]の末[すえ]に生[う]まれたこの発明[はつめい]は、努力[どりょく]の結晶[けっしょう]で＿＿なんだろう。
quiz.en: This invention, born of ten years of research, is surely the fruit of hard work.

points.title: 〜てしかるべきだ
points.meaning: should (naturally); deserves to; it's only right that
points.structure: Verb て-form + しかるべきだ / しかるべき + Noun (appropriate ...)
points.explanation:
{しかるべき} (from classical {然[しか]る} 'to be so' + {べき}) means 'appropriate, as it should be'. {〜てしかるべきだ} means 'it would be only right / natural for X to happen': {もっと評価[ひょうか]されてしかるべきだ} 'deserves to be more highly regarded'.

It's often used with passive verbs to argue that something deserves to happen but hasn't yet — giving it a slightly critical edge. With {〜てしかるべきだった}, it criticises something that should have happened.

As an adjective, {しかるべき} means 'appropriate, proper': {しかるべき措置[そち]} 'appropriate measures', {しかるべき人[ひと]} 'the proper person'. This is common in business and official language.

**Register:** formal; editorials, business, official statements.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の功績[こうせき]は、もっと評価[ひょうか]されてしかるべきだ。
examples.en: His achievements deserve far more recognition.

examples.jp: 消費者[しょうひしゃ]には、正確[せいかく]な情報[じょうほう]が提供[ていきょう]されてしかるべきだ。
examples.en: Consumers ought to be provided with accurate information.

examples.jp: 本来[ほんらい]なら、もっと早[はや]く対策[たいさく]が取[と]られてしかるべきだった。
examples.en: By rights, countermeasures should have been taken much sooner.

examples.jp: 問題[もんだい]が確認[かくにん]され次第[しだい]、しかるべき措置[そち]を講[こう]じます。
examples.en: As soon as the problem is confirmed, we will take appropriate measures.

points.notes: Compare plain {〜べきだ}: {しかるべきだ} sounds more objective, as if it's simply the natural state of things.

quiz.q: これだけ努力[どりょく]したのだから、彼女[かのじょ]は報[むく]われて＿＿。
quiz.en: She's worked so hard; she deserves to be rewarded.

quiz.q: ミスを犯[おか]した以上[いじょう]、責任者[せきにんしゃ]は＿＿処分[しょぶん]を受[う]けるべきだ。
quiz.en: Since a mistake was made, the person in charge should receive appropriate disciplinary action.

units.title: Contrast, comparison and surprise
units.summary: Comparing and contrasting at an advanced level: 'in contrast to' ({にひきかえ}), 'even more than' ({にもまして}), 'X of course, but also Y' ({もさることながら}), 'combined with' ({と相[あい]まって}), 'both X and Y' ({といい〜といい}), 'although' ({とはいえ}), 'contrary to expectation' ({と思[おも]いきや}) and 'ignoring' ({をよそに}).

points.title: 〜にひきかえ
points.meaning: in (stark) contrast to; whereas
points.structure: Noun / plain form + の + にひきかえ
points.explanation:
{〜にひきかえ} contrasts two things and shows the speaker's evaluation: one is good, the other is bad (or at least one is more favourable). 'My older brother is outgoing, whereas my younger brother is quiet.' 'Unlike last year's heatwave, this summer is pleasant.'

It is subjective — the speaker is praising one side and often criticising the other. For a neutral, factual contrast, use {〜に対[たい]して}.

**Register:** somewhat formal but heard in conversation, especially when complaining about family or colleagues.

examples.jp: 兄[あに]が社交的[しゃこうてき]なのにひきかえ、弟[おとうと]はおとなしい。
examples.en: My older brother is outgoing, whereas my younger brother is quiet.

examples.jp: 去年[きょねん]の猛暑[もうしょ]にひきかえ、今年[ことし]の夏[なつ]は過[す]ごしやすい。
examples.en: Compared with last year's heatwave, this summer is very comfortable.

examples.jp: 働[はたら]き者[もの]の妻[つま]にひきかえ、夫[おっと]は一日中[いちにちじゅう]ごろごろしている。
examples.en: Unlike his hard-working wife, the husband lazes around all day.

examples.jp: 前回[ぜんかい]の失敗[しっぱい]にひきかえ、今回[こんかい]のプロジェクトは大成功[だいせいこう]だった。
examples.en: In contrast to last time's failure, this project was a great success.

points.notes: {〜に対[たい]して} = objective contrast; {〜にひきかえ} = evaluative contrast ('one is better/worse').

quiz.q: 真面目[まじめ]な姉[あね]＿＿、妹[いもうと]は遊[あそ]んでばかりいる。
quiz.en: Unlike her serious older sister, the younger sister does nothing but play.

quiz.q: 都会[とかい]の慌[あわ]ただしい生活[せいかつ]＿＿、田舎[いなか]の暮[く]らしはのんびりしている。
quiz.en: In contrast to hectic city life, life in the countryside is relaxed.

points.title: 〜にもまして
points.meaning: even more than; above all
points.structure: Noun / question word + にもまして
points.explanation:
{増[ま]す} means 'to increase'. {X にもまして} means 'even more than X'. It compares a situation with a previous one or a normal level: {例年[れいねん]にもまして} 'even more than in a usual year', {以前[いぜん]にもまして} 'even more than before'.

With question words it means 'more than anything / anyone': {何[なに]にもまして} 'above all', {誰[だれ]にもまして} 'more than anyone'.

**Register:** formal-leaning; common in news, speeches and writing. {以前[いぜん]にもまして} and {何[なに]にもまして} are also used in careful speech.

examples.jp: 今年[ことし]の夏[なつ]は、例年[れいねん]にもまして暑[あつ]い。
examples.en: This summer is even hotter than usual.

examples.jp: 退院[たいいん]した彼[かれ]は、以前[いぜん]にもまして元気[げんき]になった。
examples.en: Since leaving hospital, he's been even livelier than before.

examples.jp: 何[なに]にもまして大切[たいせつ]なのは、家族[かぞく]の健康[けんこう]だ。
examples.en: More important than anything is my family's health.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は誰[だれ]にもまして熱心[ねっしん]に練習[れんしゅう]に取[と]り組[く]んだ。
examples.en: She threw herself into practice more enthusiastically than anyone.

points.notes: In writing you may see it in kanji: {にも増[ま]して}.

quiz.q: 再開[さいかい]されたその店[みせ]は、以前[いぜん]＿＿多[おお]くの客[きゃく]でにぎわっている。
quiz.en: Since reopening, the shop has been even busier than before.

quiz.q: 社員[しゃいん]にとって何[なに]＿＿ありがたいのは、休[やす]みが増[ふ]えることだ。
quiz.en: What employees appreciate more than anything is getting more days off.

points.title: 〜もさることながら
points.meaning: X is of course (important/good), but Y even more so
points.structure: Noun + もさることながら
points.explanation:
{〜もさることながら} acknowledges X as obviously important or impressive, then shifts focus to Y as even more notable: 'The food here is great, of course, but the service is what really stands out.'

It's a graceful, elevated way of saying {〜はもちろんだが}. Usually positive, used in praise, reviews and analysis.

**Register:** formal and written — reviews, articles, speeches, interviews. It sounds sophisticated in speech.

examples.jp: この店[みせ]は、料理[りょうり]の味[あじ]もさることながら、店員[てんいん]の接客[せっきゃく]が素晴[すば]らしい。
examples.en: The food at this restaurant is excellent, of course, but the service is truly wonderful.

examples.jp: 就職[しゅうしょく]では、学歴[がくれき]もさることながら、本人[ほんにん]のやる気[き]が重視[じゅうし]される。
examples.en: In job hunting, educational background matters, but motivation is valued even more.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は、歌[うた]の上手[うま]さもさることながら、その人柄[ひとがら]で多[おお]くのファンを魅了[みりょう]している。
examples.en: Her singing is superb, but it's her personality that has really won over so many fans.

examples.jp: 環境[かんきょう]問題[もんだい]の解決[かいけつ]には、技術[ぎじゅつ]の開発[かいはつ]もさることながら、一人[ひとり]ひとりの意識[いしき]改革[かいかく]が欠[か]かせない。
examples.en: Solving environmental problems requires new technology, of course, but changing each person's mindset is essential.

points.notes: Note the order: the 'of course' item comes first with {もさることながら}, and the main point second.

quiz.q: このホテルは、部屋[へや]からの眺[なが]め＿＿、料理[りょうり]の質[しつ]の高[たか]さで評判[ひょうばん]だ。
quiz.en: This hotel is famous for its views from the rooms, of course, but even more for the quality of its food.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]の論文[ろんぶん]は、着眼点[ちゃくがんてん]の新[あたら]しさもさること＿＿、データの正確[せいかく]さが高[たか]く評価[ひょうか]された。
quiz.en: His paper was praised for the novelty of its approach, and even more for the accuracy of its data.

points.title: 〜と相[あい]まって
points.meaning: combined with; coupled with; together with
points.structure: Noun + と相[あい]まって / Noun + も相[あい]まって
points.explanation:
{相[あい]まつ} means 'to work together, to combine'. {X と相[あい]まって Y} means 'X combined with (another factor) produced a stronger effect Y'. Two factors reinforce each other: good weather plus a holiday means huge crowds; talent plus hard work means success.

{〜も相[あい]まって} is a common variant meaning 'with X also contributing'.

**Register:** formal and written; frequent in news, reviews and analysis ({円安[えんやす]も相[あい]まって} 'helped by the weak yen').

examples.jp: 好天[こうてん]と相[あい]まって、行楽地[こうらくち]は大勢[おおぜい]の人[ひと]でにぎわった。
examples.en: Helped by the fine weather, holiday spots were crowded with people.

examples.jp: 美[うつく]しい音楽[おんがく]が映像[えいぞう]と相[あい]まって、観客[かんきゃく]を感動[かんどう]させた。
examples.en: The beautiful music, combined with the visuals, moved the audience.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の才能[さいのう]は、人一倍[ひといちばい]の努力[どりょく]と相[あい]まって、ついに花開[はなひら]いた。
examples.en: His talent, combined with exceptional effort, finally blossomed.

examples.jp: 円安[えんやす]も相[あい]まって、訪日[ほうにち]外国人[がいこくじん]の数[かず]は過去[かこ]最高[さいこう]を記録[きろく]した。
examples.en: Helped also by the weak yen, the number of foreign visitors to Japan hit a record high.

points.notes: The effect usually intensifies (good or bad). It's not used for simple listing — use {〜とともに} or {〜に加[くわ]えて} for that.

quiz.q: 紅葉[こうよう]が澄[す]んだ秋空[あきぞら]＿＿、山[やま]は息[いき]をのむほど美[うつく]しかった。
quiz.en: The autumn leaves together with the clear autumn sky made the mountains breathtakingly beautiful.

quiz.q: 景気[けいき]の回復[かいふく]も＿＿、今年[ことし]の就職[しゅうしょく]率[りつ]は大幅[おおはば]に上昇[じょうしょう]した。
quiz.en: Helped also by the economic recovery, this year's employment rate rose sharply.

points.title: 〜といい〜といい
points.meaning: both X and Y; whether you look at X or Y
points.structure: Noun₁ + といい + Noun₂ + といい
points.explanation:
{X といい Y といい} picks out two aspects (or two people) as examples, and then makes one overall judgement that applies to both — and implicitly to everything else. 'Both the size and the sunlight — this room is perfect.'

The judgement can be praise or criticism. It's the speaker's personal evaluation, so it's not used for neutral facts.

**Register:** neutral; used in conversation as well as writing. A useful way to sound natural when giving opinions.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は顔[かお]といい性格[せいかく]といい、父親[ちちおや]にそっくりだ。
examples.en: Both in looks and personality, he's just like his father.

examples.jp: デザインといい色[いろ]といい、このバッグは私[わたし]の好[この]みにぴったりだ。
examples.en: The design, the colour — this bag is exactly my taste.

examples.jp: この部屋[へや]は、広[ひろ]さといい日当[ひあ]たりといい、申[もう]し分[ぶん]ない。
examples.en: In both size and sunlight, this room leaves nothing to be desired.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]といい部長[ぶちょう]といい、この会社[かいしゃ]の幹部[かんぶ]は現場[げんば]を知[し]らない。
examples.en: The president, the department head — the executives in this company have no idea what happens on the ground.

points.notes: Similar patterns: {〜にしても〜にしても} (whether X or Y), {〜も〜も}. {〜といい〜といい} always ends in an evaluation.

quiz.q: 味[あじ]＿＿値段[ねだん]といい、この店[みせ]のランチは最高[さいこう]だ。
quiz.en: The taste, the price — this restaurant's lunch is the best.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]の作品[さくひん]は、構成[こうせい]といい表現[ひょうげん]＿＿、新人[しんじん]とは思[おも]えない出来[でき]だ。
quiz.en: In both structure and expression, her work is hard to believe as that of a newcomer.

points.title: 〜とはいえ
points.meaning: although; even though (it's true that); that said
points.structure: Noun / plain form + とはいえ / Sentence。とはいえ、…
points.explanation:
{〜とはいえ} admits that X is true, then adds that the expected consequence doesn't fully follow: 'It's spring, but mornings are still cold.' 'It's my job, but working late every night is hard.'

It can also start a sentence on its own: {とはいえ、…} 'That said, ...' — very common in writing and presentations.

**Register:** written and formal-ish, but widely used, including in careful speech. A softer, more common alternative to {といえども}.

examples.jp: 春[はる]とはいえ、朝晩[あさばん]はまだ寒[さむ]い。
examples.en: It may be spring, but mornings and evenings are still cold.

examples.jp: 仕事[しごと]とはいえ、毎晩[まいばん]遅[おそ]くまで残業[ざんぎょう]するのはつらい。
examples.en: It's my job, I know, but working late every night is tough.

examples.jp: 自分[じぶん]で選[えら]んだ道[みち]とはいえ、迷[まよ]うこともある。
examples.en: Even though it's the path I chose, I sometimes have doubts.

examples.jp: 景気[けいき]は回復[かいふく]傾向[けいこう]にある。とはいえ、まだ油断[ゆだん]はできない。
examples.en: The economy is on a recovery trend. That said, we can't let our guard down yet.

points.notes: {とはいえ} < {といえども} in formality. {とはいっても} and {といっても} are the conversational versions.

quiz.q: 三月[さんがつ]＿＿、北海道[ほっかいどう]ではまだ雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]ることがある。
quiz.en: Although it's March, it can still snow in Hokkaido.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]の言[い]うことにも一理[いちり]ある。＿＿、全面的[ぜんめんてき]に賛成[さんせい]するわけにはいかない。
quiz.en: There's some truth in what he says. That said, I can't agree with him completely.

points.title: 〜と思[おも]いきや
points.meaning: I thought X, but (to my surprise) actually Y
points.structure: plain form (often + か) + と思[おも]いきや
points.explanation:
{〜と思[おも]いきや} means 'just when I thought X — surprise! — Y'. The result is the opposite of what the speaker expected. It's often used with {〜かと思[おも]いきや}.

It describes a past event, and the second half is always a real, surprising outcome.

**Register:** originally literary, but now popular in a slightly humorous, lively way: blogs, TV narration, captions, manga and casual storytelling. It's one of the 'old' N1 forms you'll genuinely see online.

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]は休[やす]みかと思[おも]いきや、店[みせ]は開[あ]いていた。
examples.en: I thought the shop would be closed today, but it was open.

examples.jp: 試験[しけん]は簡単[かんたん]だと思[おも]いきや、最後[さいご]の問題[もんだい]がとても難[むずか]しかった。
examples.en: I thought the exam was easy, but the last question turned out to be really hard.

examples.jp: やっと仕事[しごと]が終[お]わったと思[おも]いきや、また新[あたら]しい依頼[いらい]が来[き]た。
examples.en: Just when I thought I'd finally finished work, another request came in.

examples.jp: 強豪[きょうごう]チームが勝[か]つと思[おも]いきや、無名[むめい]の高校[こうこう]が優勝[ゆうしょう]をさらった。
examples.en: Everyone expected the powerhouse team to win, but an unknown high school took the title.

points.notes: Not used for the future, or for things that went as expected.

quiz.q: 雨[あめ]が止[や]んだ＿＿、また激[はげ]しく降[ふ]り出[だ]した。
quiz.en: I thought the rain had stopped, but it started pouring again.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]のことだから遅刻[ちこく]するだろうと思[おも]い＿＿、珍[めずら]しく時間[じかん]どおりに来[き]た。
quiz.en: Knowing him, I thought he'd be late, but for once he came on time.

points.title: 〜をよそに
points.meaning: ignoring; paying no heed to; in spite of (others' concerns)
points.structure: Noun + をよそに
points.explanation:
{よそ} means 'somewhere else, outsider'. {X をよそに} means 'treating X as if it had nothing to do with oneself' — carrying on regardless of others' worry, opposition, expectations or a surrounding situation.

Typical nouns: {心配[しんぱい]}, {反対[はんたい]}, {期待[きたい]}, {批判[ひはん]}, {不安[ふあん]}, {騒[さわ]ぎ}, {不景気[ふけいき]}. There's usually a critical or ironic tone: the subject seems indifferent to what everyone else is worried about.

**Register:** written and formal; very common in news ({住民[じゅうみん]の反対[はんたい]をよそに} 'despite residents' opposition').

examples.jp: 親[おや]の心配[しんぱい]をよそに、息子[むすこ]は毎晩[まいばん]遊[あそ]び歩[ある]いている。
examples.en: Paying no attention to his parents' worries, the son goes out partying every night.

examples.jp: 住民[じゅうみん]の反対[はんたい]をよそに、工事[こうじ]は強行[きょうこう]された。
examples.en: The construction was forced through despite the residents' opposition.

examples.jp: 周囲[しゅうい]の期待[きたい]をよそに、彼[かれ]はあっさり引退[いんたい]を決[き]めた。
examples.en: Despite everyone's expectations, he casually decided to retire.

examples.jp: 不景気[ふけいき]をよそに、高級[こうきゅう]ブランドの売[う]り上[あ]げは伸[の]び続[つづ]けている。
examples.en: Despite the recession, sales of luxury brands keep growing.

points.notes: Compare {〜をものともせず} (Unit 12), which is about bravely overcoming obstacles. {をよそに} is about ignoring other people's feelings or the situation.

quiz.q: 医者[いしゃ]の忠告[ちゅうこく]＿＿、父[ちち]はタバコをやめようとしない。
quiz.en: Ignoring the doctor's advice, my father refuses to quit smoking.

quiz.q: 世間[せけん]の批判[ひはん]＿＿、政府[せいふ]は増税[ぞうぜい]に踏[ふ]み切[き]った。
quiz.en: Ignoring public criticism, the government went ahead with the tax increase.

units.title: Purpose, reason and means
units.summary: Formal ways to express purpose ({んがため}, {べく}), cause ({ゆえに}, {ばこそ}, {こととて}), pretexts ({にかこつけて}), means and formal end points ({をもって}), and acting to save face ({手前[てまえ]}).

points.title: 〜んがため(に)
points.meaning: in order to; for the sake of (with strong determination)
points.structure: Verb ない-stem + んがため(に) / んがための + Noun (する → せんがため)
points.explanation:
{〜んがため} is built from the classical volitional {ん} ('intend to') plus {がため} ('for the purpose of'). It means 'with the firm aim of doing X' and usually describes someone making great sacrifices or efforts for a goal.

Conjugation: take the nai-stem and add {んがため}: {勝[か]つ} → {勝[か]たんがため}, {生[い]きる} → {生[い]きんがため}. {する} becomes {せんがため}.

**Register:** literary and very formal — novels, historical writing, speeches, editorials. Not used in conversation; there you'd say {〜ために}.

examples.jp: 生[い]きんがために、人々[ひとびと]は必死[ひっし]で働[はたら]いた。
examples.en: People worked desperately just to survive.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は夢[ゆめ]を実現[じつげん]せんがため、全[すべ]てを犠牲[ぎせい]にした。
examples.en: He sacrificed everything to make his dream come true.

examples.jp: 真実[しんじつ]を明[あき]らかにせんがための調査[ちょうさ]が続[つづ]けられている。
examples.en: An investigation aimed at uncovering the truth is continuing.

examples.jp: 勝[か]たんがためには手段[しゅだん]を選[えら]ばないという姿勢[しせい]には、疑問[ぎもん]を感[かん]じる。
examples.en: I have doubts about an attitude of doing whatever it takes just to win.

points.notes: Not for everyday purposes like {✕パンを買[か]わんがためにコンビニへ行[い]った}. It needs a weighty goal.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は試合[しあい]に勝[か]た＿＿、毎日[まいにち]厳[きび]しい練習[れんしゅう]を続[つづ]けた。
quiz.en: Determined to win the match, he kept up harsh training every day.

quiz.q: 会社[かいしゃ]は利益[りえき]を上[あ]げ＿＿ため、従業員[じゅうぎょういん]の安全[あんぜん]を軽視[けいし]していた。
quiz.en: In its drive to make a profit, the company had neglected the safety of its workers.

points.title: 〜べく
points.meaning: in order to; with the aim of
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + べく (する → すべく／するべく)
points.explanation:
{べく} is the continuative form of {べし} (see Unit 14). {〜べく} means 'in order to do X' and shows a deliberate purpose. It is much more common than {んがため}, especially in the news: companies act {〜すべく}, committees are set up {〜すべく}, volunteers gather {〜すべく}.

The second half is a concrete action taken to achieve the goal.

**Register:** formal and written; frequent in news, business reports and press releases. Also heard in formal speeches.

examples.jp: 被災地[ひさいち]を支援[しえん]すべく、多[おお]くのボランティアが集[あつ]まった。
examples.en: Many volunteers gathered to support the disaster-hit area.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は弁護士[べんごし]になるべく、毎日[まいにち]十時間[じゅうじかん]勉強[べんきょう]している。
examples.en: He studies ten hours a day with the aim of becoming a lawyer.

examples.jp: 真相[しんそう]を究明[きゅうめい]すべく、調査[ちょうさ]委員会[いいんかい]が設置[せっち]された。
examples.en: An investigative committee was set up to get to the bottom of the matter.

examples.jp: 同社[どうしゃ]は海外[かいがい]市場[しじょう]に進出[しんしゅつ]すべく、現地[げんち]企業[きぎょう]との提携[ていけい]を進[すす]めている。
examples.en: The company is pursuing partnerships with local firms in order to expand into overseas markets.

points.notes: Related forms: {〜べくして} 'as was bound to happen' ({起[お]こるべくして起[お]こった事故[じこ]}) and {〜べくもない} 'there's no way to' ({知[し]るべくもない}). Not for requests or commands in the second half.

quiz.q: 留学[りゅうがく]の費用[ひよう]を貯[た]める＿＿、彼女[かのじょ]はアルバイトを三[みっ]つ掛[か]け持[も]ちしている。
quiz.en: To save money for studying abroad, she's working three part-time jobs.

quiz.q: 事故[じこ]の原因[げんいん]を明[あき]らかに＿＿、専門家[せんもんか]による調査[ちょうさ]が始[はじ]まった。
quiz.en: An investigation by experts has begun in order to determine the cause of the accident.

points.title: 〜ゆえ(に)／〜がゆえに
points.meaning: because of; due to; therefore
points.structure: Noun (の) + ゆえ(に) / plain form + (が)ゆえに / Noun + ゆえの + Noun
points.explanation:
{ゆえ} ({故[ゆえ]}) is a classical word for 'reason'. {〜ゆえ(に)} means 'because of X' and sounds logical, weighty or literary. {〜がゆえに} after a clause is common in essays: {不便[ふべん]であるがゆえに} 'precisely because it is inconvenient'.

As a sentence connector, {ゆえに} means 'therefore' — used in logic and mathematics. And Descartes' famous line is {我[われ]思[おも]う、ゆえに我[われ]あり} 'I think, therefore I am'.

**Register:** written, academic and literary. {若[わか]さゆえの過[あやま]ち} 'a mistake of youth' is a well-known phrase.

examples.jp: 若[わか]さゆえの過[あやま]ちは、誰[だれ]にでもある。
examples.en: Everyone makes mistakes because they're young.

examples.jp: 我[われ]思[おも]う、ゆえに我[われ]あり。
examples.en: I think, therefore I am.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は貧[まず]しさゆえに、学校[がっこう]に通[かよ]うことができなかった。
examples.en: Because of poverty, he was unable to attend school.

examples.jp: この地域[ちいき]は交通[こうつう]が不便[ふべん]であるがゆえに、若者[わかもの]の流出[りゅうしゅつ]が続[つづ]いている。
examples.en: Because transport in this region is so inconvenient, young people keep leaving.

points.notes: In conversation, use {〜から} or {〜ので}. {〜ゆえ} without {に} is even more literary.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]は正直[しょうじき]すぎる＿＿、時々[ときどき]人[ひと]を傷[きず]つけてしまう。
quiz.en: Because she's too honest, she sometimes ends up hurting people.

quiz.q: 子[こ]どもを思[おも]う＿＿の厳[きび]しさだということは、大人[おとな]になってから分[わ]かった。
quiz.en: It was only after I grew up that I understood that the strictness came from caring about the child.

points.title: 〜ばこそ
points.meaning: precisely because; it is only because
points.structure: Verb / Adjective ば-form + こそ (Noun / な-adj + であればこそ)
points.explanation:
{〜ばこそ} is an emphatic 'because'. It insists that X is the true reason — often a reason the listener may not have realised. 'I say harsh things *because* I care about you.'

It usually explains a positive motive behind something that might look negative (strictness, criticism, sacrifice), or highlights an essential precondition. The sentence often ends in {〜のだ}.

**Register:** formal and slightly literary, but used in heartfelt speech. Similar in meaning to {〜からこそ}, which is far more common in conversation.

examples.jp: あなたのことを思[おも]えばこそ、厳[きび]しいことを言[い]うのです。
examples.en: It's precisely because I care about you that I'm being harsh.

examples.jp: 健康[けんこう]であればこそ、好[す]きな仕事[しごと]を続[つづ]けられる。
examples.en: It's only because I'm healthy that I can keep doing the work I love.

examples.jp: 家族[かぞく]の支[ささ]えがあればこそ、ここまで頑張[がんば]ってこられた。
examples.en: It's only because of my family's support that I've been able to keep going this far.

examples.jp: 信頼[しんらい]していればこそ、彼[かれ]に大事[だいじ]な仕事[しごと]を任[まか]せたのだ。
examples.en: It's precisely because I trust him that I entrusted him with such important work.

points.notes: Not used for negative reasons: {✕寝坊[ねぼう]すればこそ遅刻[ちこく]した}. Use {〜からこそ} in everyday talk.

quiz.q: 君[きみ]に期待[きたい]して＿＿、こうして注意[ちゅうい]しているんだ。
quiz.en: It's precisely because I have high hopes for you that I'm warning you like this.

quiz.q: 愛[あい]して＿＿、別[わか]れを選[えら]んだのだ。
quiz.en: It was precisely because I loved her that I chose to part.

points.title: 〜こととて
points.meaning: because; since (as an excuse or apology)
points.structure: Verb / Adjective (plain) + こととて / Noun + の + こととて
points.explanation:
{〜こととて} gives a reason, usually as an excuse when apologising or asking for forgiveness: 'Since it was my first time, please forgive any shortcomings.' 'Since it was done by a child, please let it go.'

It can also simply state a circumstance: {休日[きゅうじつ]のこととて} 'it being a holiday'. A typical lead-in is {何分[なにぶん]} 'after all, you see'.

**Register:** old-fashioned and very formal; seen in letters, formal apologies and historical novels. You'll rarely hear it today, but it appears on the JLPT and in very polite business apologies.

examples.jp: 慣[な]れないこととて、ご迷惑[めいわく]をおかけしました。
examples.en: I'm sorry for the trouble; I'm not used to this.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どものしたこととて、どうか許[ゆる]してやってください。
examples.en: It was done by a child, so please forgive him.

examples.jp: 休日[きゅうじつ]のこととて、役所[やくしょ]はどこも閉[し]まっていた。
examples.en: It being a holiday, all the government offices were closed.

examples.jp: 何分[なにぶん]初[はじ]めてのこととて、至[いた]らない点[てん]もあるかと存[ぞん]じます。
examples.en: As this is, after all, my first time, I expect there will be some shortcomings.

points.notes: Don't confuse it with {〜とて} 'even' ({子[こ]どもとて容赦[ようしゃ]しない} 'won't show mercy even to a child').

quiz.q: 不慣[ふな]れな＿＿、手続[てつづ]きに時間[じかん]がかかってしまい申[もう]し訳[わけ]ありません。
quiz.en: I'm sorry the procedure took so long; I'm not used to it.

quiz.q: 何[なに]しろ急[きゅう]な＿＿、十分[じゅうぶん]な準備[じゅんび]ができませんでした。
quiz.en: As it was so sudden, we couldn't prepare sufficiently.

points.title: 〜にかこつけて
points.meaning: using X as an excuse / pretext
points.structure: Noun + にかこつけて
points.explanation:
{かこつける} means 'to use as a pretext'. {X にかこつけて Y} means 'using X as an excuse, someone does Y (what they really wanted to do)'. Dad goes out drinking every night 'for work socialising'; someone goes sightseeing 'on a business trip'.

The tone is critical or self-mocking: the stated reason isn't the real one.

**Register:** neutral; used in conversation and writing. Fairly common in real life, especially when teasing someone.

examples.jp: 出張[しゅっちょう]にかこつけて、観光[かんこう]を楽[たの]しんできた。
examples.en: I used the business trip as an excuse to do some sightseeing.

examples.jp: 父[ちち]は付[つ]き合[あ]いにかこつけて、毎晩[まいばん]飲[の]みに行[い]く。
examples.en: My father goes drinking every night under the pretext of socialising for work.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は体調[たいちょう]不良[ふりょう]にかこつけて、面倒[めんどう]な会議[かいぎ]を欠席[けっせき]した。
examples.en: He used feeling unwell as an excuse to skip the tedious meeting.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもの誕生日[たんじょうび]にかこつけて、自分[じぶん]が欲[ほ]しかったゲームを買[か]った。
examples.en: Using my child's birthday as an excuse, I bought a game I'd wanted myself.

points.notes: Similar: {〜を口実[こうじつ]に} 'using X as a pretext'. {かこつけて} implies the excuse is thin.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は仕事[しごと]が忙[いそが]しいこと＿＿、家事[かじ]を全[まった]く手伝[てつだ]わない。
quiz.en: Using his busy job as an excuse, he doesn't help with the housework at all.

quiz.q: 打[う]ち合[あ]わせ＿＿、取引先[とりひきさき]の近[ちか]くの有名[ゆうめい]なラーメン屋[や]に行[い]ってきた。
quiz.en: Using the client meeting as an excuse, I went to a famous ramen shop near their office.

points.title: 〜をもって
points.meaning: (1) by means of; with; (2) as of (formal end point)
points.structure: Noun + をもって / をもちまして (more polite) / をもってすれば
points.explanation:
{〜をもって} is a formal particle with two main uses:

**1. Means or method:** 'by means of, with' — {書面[しょめん]をもって} 'in writing', {身[み]をもって} 'personally, first-hand', {実力[じつりょく]をもってすれば} 'with (his) ability, (anything is possible)'.

**2. Time limit / end point:** 'as of, with X (it ends)' — {本日[ほんじつ]をもちまして閉店[へいてん]いたします} 'we close as of today'; {以上[いじょう]をもちまして} 'with that, (we conclude)'.

**Register:** very formal. Use 2 is everywhere in Japanese working life: meeting chairs say {以上[いじょう]をもちまして、本日[ほんじつ]の会議[かいぎ]を終了[しゅうりょう]いたします}, and shops post closure notices with it. Worth knowing actively.

examples.jp: 以上[いじょう]をもちまして、本日[ほんじつ]の会議[かいぎ]を終了[しゅうりょう]いたします。
examples.en: With that, we conclude today's meeting.

examples.jp: 試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]は、書面[しょめん]をもってお知[し]らせします。
examples.en: You will be notified of the exam results in writing.

examples.jp: 本日[ほんじつ]をもちまして、当店[とうてん]は閉店[へいてん]いたします。
examples.en: As of today, this shop will be closing.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の実力[じつりょく]をもってすれば、優勝[ゆうしょう]も夢[ゆめ]ではない。
examples.en: With his ability, winning the championship isn't just a dream.

points.notes: {〜を限[かぎ]りに} (Unit 1) is similar to use 2 but emphasises 'this is the last time'; {〜をもって} is the more official, neutral announcement.

quiz.q: 合否[ごうひ]の結果[けっか]は、メール＿＿ご連絡[れんらく]いたします。
quiz.en: We will notify you by email of whether you passed or failed.

quiz.q: 三月[さんがつ]三十一日[さんじゅういちにち]＿＿、本[ほん]サービスの提供[ていきょう]を終了[しゅうりょう]いたします。
quiz.en: As of March 31, we will discontinue this service.

points.title: 〜手前[てまえ]
points.meaning: because of (one's position / what one has said); in front of (so as not to lose face)
points.structure: Verb (plain, often た-form) + 手前[てまえ] / Noun + の + 手前[てまえ]
points.explanation:
{手前[てまえ]} literally means 'in front of oneself'. As grammar, it describes a constraint of face: because of what you've said or done, or because certain people are watching, you can't act a certain way. 'Having boasted that I'd win, I can't lose now.' 'In front of my kids, I can't break my promise.'

The second half is usually {〜わけにはいかない}, {〜なければならない} or {〜とは言[い]えない}.

**Register:** neutral to slightly formal; genuinely used in conversation. Very relevant to Japanese social life, where saving face matters.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもの手前[てまえ]、親[おや]が約束[やくそく]を破[やぶ]るわけにはいかない。
examples.en: In front of the children, parents can't break their promises.

examples.jp: 大口[おおぐち]をたたいた手前[てまえ]、負[ま]けるわけにはいかない。
examples.en: After all my big talk, I can't afford to lose.

examples.jp: 部下[ぶか]の手前[てまえ]、上司[じょうし]として弱音[よわね]を吐[は]くわけにはいかない。
examples.en: With my subordinates watching, I can't complain as their boss.

examples.jp: 「必[かなら]ず成功[せいこう]させる」と言[い]ってしまった手前[てまえ]、今更[いまさら]やめるとは言[い]えない。
examples.en: Having said 'I'll definitely make it succeed', I can't say I'm quitting now.

points.notes: {手前[てまえ]} also simply means 'just before (a place)': {駅[えき]の手前[てまえ]} 'just before the station'. Context makes it clear.

quiz.q: みんなの前[まえ]で「絶対[ぜったい]に合格[ごうかく]する」と宣言[せんげん]した＿＿、落[お]ちるわけにはいかない。
quiz.en: Having declared in front of everyone that I'll definitely pass, I can't fail.

quiz.q: 後輩[こうはい]の＿＿、先輩[せんぱい]の私[わたし]が泣[な]き言[ごと]を言[い]うわけにはいかない。
quiz.en: With my juniors watching, I, as their senior, can't go whining.

units.title: Attitude, manner and standards
units.summary: Describing how people act and what they act according to: 'as if to say' ({とばかりに}, {んばかり}), complaining about someone ({ときたら}), defying obstacles ({をものともせず}), 'in one's own way' ({なりに}), 'in line with' ({に即[そく]して}), saying things boldly ({てはばからない}) and doing things absent-mindedly ({ともなく}).

points.title: 〜とばかりに
points.meaning: as if to say; as though (X)
points.structure: Quotation / plain form (often a command or volitional) + とばかりに
points.explanation:
{〜とばかりに} describes an action that silently communicates a message: someone doesn't actually say X, but their behaviour all but says it. 'He turned his back on me as if to say "Go home".'

The X is often a short quote, command or exclamation: {早[はや]く帰[かえ]れ}, {待[ま]ってました}, {いい加減[かげん]にしろ}. The fixed phrase {ここぞとばかりに} means 'seizing the moment, as if to say "this is it!"'.

It describes other people's actions, not your own.

**Register:** written and narrative, but also common in vivid storytelling and TV narration.

examples.jp: 待[ま]ってましたとばかりに、子[こ]どもたちはプールに飛[と]び込[こ]んだ。
examples.en: As if they'd been waiting for that moment, the children leapt into the pool.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は「もう帰[かえ]れ」とばかりに、私[わたし]に背[せ]を向[む]けた。
examples.en: He turned his back on me as if to say, 'Go home.'

examples.jp: 店員[てんいん]は早[はや]く出[で]て行[い]けとばかりに、閉店[へいてん]の準備[じゅんび]を始[はじ]めた。
examples.en: The shop staff started getting ready to close, as if to say 'Hurry up and leave.'

examples.jp: ここぞとばかりに、彼[かれ]は日頃[ひごろ]の不満[ふまん]をぶちまけた。
examples.en: Seizing his chance, he poured out all his usual complaints.

points.notes: Compare {〜んばかり} (next point): {とばかりに} follows a quote; {んばかり} follows a verb stem and means 'almost doing'. {言[い]わんばかりに} and {とばかりに} are often interchangeable.

quiz.q: 母[はは]は「いい加減[かげん]にしなさい」＿＿、テレビを消[け]した。
quiz.en: My mother switched off the TV as if to say, 'That's enough!'

quiz.q: セールが始[はじ]まると、客[きゃく]たちはここぞ＿＿売[う]り場[ば]に殺到[さっとう]した。
quiz.en: When the sale began, the customers seized their moment and rushed to the counters.

points.title: 〜んばかり
points.meaning: almost; as if about to; on the verge of
points.structure: Verb ない-stem + んばかり(に／の／だ) (する → せんばかり)
points.explanation:
{〜んばかり} combines classical volitional {ん} with {ばかり}: 'just about to do X'. It describes something so intense it seems to be on the verge of X, though X doesn't actually happen: {泣[な]き出[だ]さんばかり} 'on the verge of tears', {割[わ]れんばかりの拍手[はくしゅ]} 'thunderous applause (as if the hall would split)'.

{言[い]わんばかりに} 'as if to say' is extremely common: {帰[かえ]れと言[い]わんばかりに}.

**Register:** literary and descriptive — novels, news, sports commentary. {割[わ]れんばかりの拍手[はくしゅ]} and {言[い]わんばかり} are set phrases worth learning.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は泣[な]き出[だ]さんばかりの顔[かお]で、私[わたし]を見[み]つめた。
examples.en: She stared at me, looking as if she was about to burst into tears.

examples.jp: 優勝[ゆうしょう]が決[き]まった瞬間[しゅんかん]、会場[かいじょう]は割[わ]れんばかりの拍手[はくしゅ]に包[つつ]まれた。
examples.en: The moment the victory was decided, the venue erupted in thunderous applause.

examples.jp: 店主[てんしゅ]は、二度[にど]と来[く]るなと言[い]わんばかりに、私[わたし]たちをにらんだ。
examples.en: The shop owner glared at us as if to say 'Never come back.'

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は今[いま]にも殴[なぐ]りかからんばかりの勢[いきお]いで怒鳴[どな]った。
examples.en: He yelled as though he were about to throw a punch at any moment.

points.notes: Forms: {〜んばかりに} + verb, {〜んばかりの} + noun, {〜んばかりだ} at the end of a sentence.

quiz.q: コンサートの最後[さいご]に、会場[かいじょう]は割[わ]れ＿＿拍手[はくしゅ]に包[つつ]まれた。
quiz.en: At the end of the concert, the hall was filled with thunderous applause.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は「お前[まえ]が悪[わる]い」と言[い]わ＿＿、私[わたし]をにらみつけた。
quiz.en: He glared at me as if to say 'It's your fault.'

points.title: 〜ときたら
points.meaning: speaking of X (exasperated); when it comes to X (complaint)
points.structure: Noun + ときたら
points.explanation:
{〜ときたら} raises a topic in order to complain about it. The topic is usually someone close (husband, kids, boss) or something annoying (the weather, an old computer), and what follows is a criticism or expression of frustration.

It's very subjective and emotional: 'My husband, honestly — he just sleeps all day on his days off.'

**Register:** conversational! Unlike most N1 grammar, you'll genuinely hear this in everyday chat, especially among friends and in TV dramas. It's not used in formal writing. It also has a less common positive use with food and drink ({夏[なつ]のビールときたら最高[さいこう]だ}).

examples.jp: この古[ふる]いパソコンときたら、すぐ固[かた]まるんだから。
examples.en: This old computer, honestly — it freezes all the time.

examples.jp: うちの夫[おっと]ときたら、休[やす]みの日[ひ]は一日中[いちにちじゅう]寝[ね]てばかりいる。
examples.en: My husband, I tell you — on his days off he just sleeps all day.

examples.jp: あの店[みせ]の店員[てんいん]ときたら、客[きゃく]が来[き]ても挨拶[あいさつ]一[ひと]つしない。
examples.en: The staff at that shop don't even say hello when customers come in.

examples.jp: 最近[さいきん]の天気[てんき]ときたら、暑[あつ]かったり寒[さむ]かったりで本当[ほんとう]に困[こま]る。
examples.en: The weather lately — hot one day, cold the next. It's really annoying.

points.notes: Not for yourself, and not for neutral topics. For a neutral 'speaking of', use {〜といえば}.

quiz.q: うちの息子[むすこ]＿＿、ゲームばかりして全然[ぜんぜん]勉強[べんきょう]しない。
quiz.en: My son, honestly — he does nothing but play games and never studies.

quiz.q: あの政治家[せいじか]＿＿、言[い]うことがころころ変[か]わる。
quiz.en: That politician, honestly — what he says changes all the time.

points.title: 〜をものともせず(に)
points.meaning: undaunted by; in defiance of; making light of
points.structure: Noun (obstacle) + をものともせず(に)
points.explanation:
{〜をものともせず} means 'not treating X as anything to worry about' — bravely pushing through difficulties: injury, storms, opposition, danger. It expresses admiration for the person's courage or determination.

It describes others (or a group) from an observer's point of view, so it's not used to describe yourself.

**Register:** written and formal; very common in news and sports reporting ({けがをものともせず} 'shrugging off an injury').

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は足[あし]のけがをものともせず、最後[さいご]まで走[はし]り抜[ぬ]いた。
examples.en: Undaunted by his leg injury, he ran all the way to the finish.

examples.jp: 周囲[しゅうい]の反対[はんたい]をものともせずに、彼女[かのじょ]は起業[きぎょう]した。
examples.en: Brushing aside the opposition of those around her, she started her own business.

examples.jp: 救助隊[きゅうじょたい]は激[はげ]しい雨[あめ]をものともせず、行方[ゆくえ]不明者[ふめいしゃ]の捜索[そうさく]を続[つづ]けた。
examples.en: Undeterred by the heavy rain, the rescue team continued searching for the missing.

examples.jp: 数々[かずかず]の困難[こんなん]をものともせず、二人[ふたり]は夢[ゆめ]を実現[じつげん]させた。
examples.en: Overcoming countless difficulties, the two of them made their dream come true.

points.notes: {をものともせず} = admirable courage against obstacles; {をよそに} (Unit 10) = ignoring other people's worries, often critical.

quiz.q: その登山家[とざんか]は、零下[れいか]三十度[さんじゅうど]の寒[さむ]さ＿＿、頂上[ちょうじょう]を目指[めざ]した。
quiz.en: Undaunted by the cold of minus thirty degrees, the climber pushed on toward the summit.

quiz.q: 選手[せんしゅ]たちは強風[きょうふう]をものとも＿＿、全力[ぜんりょく]でプレーした。
quiz.en: Undeterred by the strong wind, the players gave it their all.

points.title: 〜なりに／〜なりの
points.meaning: in one's own way; as best one can (given one's limits)
points.structure: Noun / plain form + なりに (+ Verb) / なりの (+ Noun)
points.explanation:
{〜なりに} means 'in a way that suits X, within X's limits'. It acknowledges that X isn't perfect or fully capable, but still makes an effort or has a valid perspective: {子[こ]どもは子[こ]どもなりに} 'kids, in their own way', {私[わたし]なりに考[かんが]えた} 'I thought about it as best I could'.

Repeating the noun ({子[こ]どもは子[こ]どもなりに}) is very common. {〜なりの} modifies a noun: {彼[かれ]なりの理由[りゆう]} 'his own reasons'.

**Register:** neutral and very common in everyday conversation and business. {私[わたし]なりに} is a humble, useful phrase for meetings: 'here's my take'.

examples.jp: 私[わたし]なりに考[かんが]えてみたのですが、この案[あん]はどうでしょうか。
examples.en: I've given it some thought in my own way — how about this idea?

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]には彼[かれ]なりの事情[じじょう]があるのだろう。
examples.en: He probably has his own reasons.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもは子[こ]どもなりに、親[おや]のことを心配[しんぱい]しているものだ。
examples.en: Children worry about their parents in their own way.

examples.jp: 給料[きゅうりょう]は少[すく]ないが、少[すく]ないなりに工夫[くふう]して生活[せいかつ]している。
examples.en: My salary is small, but I get by with a bit of ingenuity.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {ならでは} 'unique to' (Unit 6) — {ならでは} is high praise; {なりに} admits limitations. Also different from {なり} 'as soon as' (Unit 1).

quiz.q: 新人[しんじん]は新人[しんじん]＿＿、精一杯[せいいっぱい]頑張[がんば]っている。
quiz.en: The newcomers are doing their best in their own way.

quiz.q: 結果[けっか]は出[で]なかったが、自分[じぶん]＿＿努力[どりょく]はしたつもりだ。
quiz.en: I didn't get results, but I believe I made an effort in my own way.

points.title: 〜に即[そく]して／〜に即[そく]した
points.meaning: in line with; in accordance with (facts, reality, rules)
points.structure: Noun + に即[そく]して (+ Verb) / に即[そく]した (+ Noun)
points.explanation:
{即[そく]する} means 'to conform to, to be based on'. {X に即[そく]して} means 'closely following X' — where X is facts, reality, actual conditions, experience or rules: {事実[じじつ]に即[そく]して} 'based on the facts', {実情[じつじょう]に即[そく]した政策[せいさく]} 'policy suited to actual conditions'.

The idea is matching a plan or explanation to concrete reality, rather than theory.

**Register:** formal; very common in business, government and academic writing. Also written {則[そく]して} when the standard is a rule or law.

examples.jp: 事実[じじつ]に即[そく]して、事故[じこ]の経緯[けいい]を説明[せつめい]してください。
examples.en: Please explain how the accident happened, sticking to the facts.

examples.jp: 実情[じつじょう]に即[そく]した政策[せいさく]が求[もと]められている。
examples.en: Policies that reflect the actual situation are needed.

examples.jp: 規則[きそく]に即[そく]して処理[しょり]しなければならない。
examples.en: This must be handled in accordance with the rules.

examples.jp: 学生[がくせい]のレベルに即[そく]した教材[きょうざい]を使[つか]うべきだ。
examples.en: We should use teaching materials suited to the students' level.

points.notes: Similar: {〜に沿[そ]って} (along the lines of) and {〜に基[もと]づいて} (based on). {に即[そく]して} stresses close fit with reality.

quiz.q: 法律[ほうりつ]は、時代[じだい]の変化[へんか]＿＿見直[みなお]されるべきだ。
quiz.en: Laws should be revised in line with the changing times.

quiz.q: 机上[きじょう]の空論[くうろん]ではなく、現場[げんば]の実態[じったい]に＿＿対策[たいさく]が必要[ひつよう]だ。
quiz.en: We need measures that match the reality on the ground, not armchair theories.

points.title: 〜てはばからない
points.meaning: to not hesitate to (say); to boldly / shamelessly (declare)
points.structure: Verb て-form (言[い]う・公言[こうげん]する etc.) + はばからない
points.explanation:
{はばかる} means 'to hold back out of consideration or fear'. {〜てはばからない} means 'to say or do X openly, without any hesitation' — even though others might find it bold, arrogant or controversial.

It mostly combines with verbs of speaking: {言[い]う}, {公言[こうげん]する} (declare publicly), {断言[だんげん]する} (assert), {口[くち]にする}. Depending on context, it can sound admiring (confident) or critical (shameless).

**Register:** written and formal — news, profiles, criticism.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は「自分[じぶん]は天才[てんさい]だ」と公言[こうげん]してはばからない。
examples.en: He openly declares that he's a genius.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は、仕事[しごと]より家族[かぞく]が大事[だいじ]だと言[い]ってはばからない。
examples.en: She doesn't hesitate to say that her family matters more than her work.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]は「失敗[しっぱい]を恐[おそ]れるな」と口[くち]にしてはばからない。
examples.en: The president never hesitates to say, 'Don't be afraid of failure.'

examples.jp: その政治家[せいじか]は、差別的[さべつてき]な発言[はつげん]を繰[く]り返[かえ]してはばからない。
examples.en: That politician shamelessly keeps making discriminatory remarks.

points.notes: Related: {人目[ひとめ]をはばからず} 'without caring who's watching' ({人目[ひとめ]をはばからず泣[な]いた} 'cried openly in front of everyone').

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は自分[じぶん]こそが次[つぎ]の社長[しゃちょう]にふさわしいと言[い]って＿＿。
quiz.en: He openly says that he's the one best suited to be the next president.

quiz.q: その評論家[ひょうろんか]は、日本[にほん]映画[えいが]は世界一[せかいいち]だと公言[こうげん]して＿＿。
quiz.en: The critic openly declares that Japanese cinema is the best in the world.

points.title: 〜ともなく／〜ともなしに
points.meaning: without really meaning to; absent-mindedly; from somewhere (unknown)
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ともなく + same verb / Question word (+ particle) + ともなく
points.explanation:
{〜ともなく} has two uses:

**1. Verb + {ともなく} + same verb:** doing something without any particular intention, absent-mindedly: {見[み]るともなく見[み]ていた} 'was half-watching', {聞[き]くともなしに聞[き]いていた} 'overheard without really listening'. Usually with perception verbs (see, hear, think).

**2. Question word + {ともなく}:** the source is unclear: {どこからともなく} 'from somewhere or other', {誰[だれ]からともなく} 'without anyone in particular starting it', {いつからともなく} 'at some point'.

**Register:** literary and descriptive — novels, essays. {どこからともなく} is common in storytelling generally.

examples.jp: どこからともなく、いい匂[にお]いが漂[ただよ]ってきた。
examples.en: A lovely smell came drifting from somewhere.

examples.jp: 見[み]るともなくテレビを見[み]ていたら、昔[むかし]の友人[ゆうじん]が映[うつ]っていた。
examples.en: I was half-watching TV when an old friend appeared on the screen.

examples.jp: 聞[き]くともなしに隣[となり]の席[せき]の会話[かいわ]を聞[き]いていた。
examples.en: Without really meaning to, I was listening to the conversation at the next table.

examples.jp: 誰[だれ]からともなく拍手[はくしゅ]が起[お]こり、やがて会場[かいじょう]全体[ぜんたい]に広[ひろ]がった。
examples.en: Applause started from no one in particular and soon spread through the whole hall.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {ともなると} 'when it comes to' (Unit 6).

quiz.q: 窓[まど]の外[そと]を眺[なが]める＿＿眺[なが]めていると、一羽[いちわ]の鳥[とり]が飛[と]んできた。
quiz.en: As I was absent-mindedly gazing out of the window, a bird flew over.

quiz.q: どこから＿＿、子[こ]どもたちの歌声[うたごえ]が聞[き]こえてきた。
quiz.en: From somewhere, the sound of children singing reached us.

units.title: Extremes, limits and prohibitions
units.summary: Reaching an extreme stage ({に至[いた]って}, {に至[いた]るまで}), 'only' ({ただ〜のみ}), moral and formal prohibitions ({まじき}, {べからず}), 'whether or not' ({〜うが〜まいが}), 'want to but can't' ({〜うにも〜ない}) and 'it's not as if' ({ではあるまいし}).

points.title: 〜に至[いた]って／〜に至[いた]っては
points.meaning: only when (things) reached X; as for X (the most extreme case)
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) / Noun + に至[いた]って(は／も)
points.explanation:
{至[いた]る} means 'to reach, to arrive at'. Three related forms:

- **{〜に至[いた]って}** — 'only when things reached the stage of X (did something finally happen)'. Usually criticises a late reaction: {死者[ししゃ]が出[で]るに至[いた]って、ようやく…} 'only once people had died did they finally...'.
- **{〜に至[いた]っても}** — 'even when it reached X, still (no change)'.
- **{〜に至[いた]っては}** — after listing examples, introduces the most extreme one: 'as for X, it's even worse'. {父[ちち]に至[いた]っては口[くち]もきいてくれない} 'and my father — he won't even speak to me'.

**Register:** formal and written; common in news, editorials and reports.

examples.jp: 事態[じたい]が深刻[しんこく]になるに至[いた]って、政府[せいふ]はようやく対策[たいさく]に乗[の]り出[だ]した。
examples.en: Only when the situation became serious did the government finally take action.

examples.jp: 死者[ししゃ]が出[で]るに至[いた]っても、会社[かいしゃ]は責任[せきにん]を認[みと]めなかった。
examples.en: Even after people had died, the company still didn't admit responsibility.

examples.jp: 家族[かぞく]は全員[ぜんいん]反対[はんたい]した。父[ちち]に至[いた]っては、口[くち]もきいてくれない。
examples.en: My whole family was against it. My father won't even speak to me.

examples.jp: 今年[ことし]は不作[ふさく]で米[こめ]の値段[ねだん]が上[あ]がった。野菜[やさい]に至[いた]っては、去年[きょねん]の倍[ばい]だ。
examples.en: Because of the poor harvest, rice prices went up this year. As for vegetables, they're double last year's price.

points.notes: Also the set phrase {〜に至[いた]った} 'it came to the point of X' in formal statements: {辞任[じにん]するに至[いた]った}.

quiz.q: 工場[こうじょう]の排水[はいすい]で住民[じゅうみん]に健康[けんこう]被害[ひがい]が出[で]る＿＿、ようやく調査[ちょうさ]が始[はじ]まった。
quiz.en: Only when the factory's wastewater began causing health problems for residents did an investigation finally begin.

quiz.q: 社員[しゃいん]の多[おお]くが残業[ざんぎょう]に不満[ふまん]を持[も]っている。営業部[えいぎょうぶ]＿＿、月[つき]百時間[ひゃくじかん]を超[こ]える人[ひと]もいる。
quiz.en: Many employees are unhappy about overtime. In the sales department, some people even exceed a hundred hours a month.

points.title: 〜に至[いた]るまで
points.meaning: (all the way) to; down to; even
points.structure: Noun + に至[いた]るまで / Noun₁ + から + Noun₂ + に至[いた]るまで
points.explanation:
{〜に至[いた]るまで} stresses that a range extends all the way to an extreme or surprising point: {食器[しょっき]から家具[かぐ]に至[いた]るまで} 'everything from tableware right down to furniture'. It's typically paired with {〜から}, and the last item is the most unexpected or detailed.

With time words, {現在[げんざい]に至[いた]るまで} means 'right up to the present'.

**Register:** formal; common in writing, advertising, news and formal speech. A more emphatic version of {〜まで}.

examples.jp: この店[みせ]では、食器[しょっき]から家具[かぐ]に至[いた]るまで、すべて手作[てづく]りだ。
examples.en: Everything in this shop, from the tableware to the furniture, is handmade.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の小説[しょうせつ]は、子[こ]どもから高齢者[こうれいしゃ]に至[いた]るまで、幅広[はばひろ]く読[よ]まれている。
examples.en: His novels are widely read by everyone from children to the elderly.

examples.jp: 校則[こうそく]は、髪型[かみがた]から靴下[くつした]の色[いろ]に至[いた]るまで細[こま]かく決[き]められている。
examples.en: The school rules specify everything in detail, from hairstyles right down to the colour of your socks.

examples.jp: 事故[じこ]の原因[げんいん]については、現在[げんざい]に至[いた]るまで明[あき]らかになっていない。
examples.en: The cause of the accident remains unclear to this day.

points.notes: Emphasises completeness ('everything, even the smallest details'). Compare {〜にわたって} 'over (a period / area)'.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]の部屋[へや]は、本棚[ほんだな]から机[つくえ]の引[ひ]き出[だ]しの中[なか]＿＿、きちんと整理[せいり]されている。
quiz.en: His room is neatly organised, from the bookshelves all the way down to the inside of the desk drawers.

quiz.q: この問題[もんだい]は、発生[はっせい]から十年[じゅうねん]たった今日[こんにち]に＿＿解決[かいけつ]されていない。
quiz.en: Even today, ten years after it arose, this problem has still not been solved.

points.title: ただ〜のみ
points.meaning: only; solely; nothing but
points.structure: ただ + Noun / Verb (dictionary form) + のみ
points.explanation:
{のみ} is the formal, written equivalent of {だけ} 'only'. Adding {ただ} in front strengthens it: 'nothing but X'. A very common use is at the end of a sentence: {あとはただ結果[けっか]を待[ま]つのみだ} 'all that's left is to wait for the results' — expressing resignation, determination or prayer.

{ただ〜のみならず} means 'not only... but also' (formal {だけでなく}).

**Register:** formal and written — speeches, statements, news, essays. {〜を祈[いの]るのみです} is common in formal condolences and messages of support.

examples.jp: ここまで来[き]たら、あとはただ結果[けっか]を待[ま]つのみだ。
examples.en: Now that it's come this far, all we can do is wait for the result.

examples.jp: 今[いま]はただ、皆様[みなさま]のご無事[ぶじ]を祈[いの]るのみです。
examples.en: All I can do now is pray for everyone's safety.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]はただ自分[じぶん]の利益[りえき]のみを考[かんが]えている。
examples.en: He thinks only of his own interests.

examples.jp: 津波[つなみ]の後[あと]、海岸[かいがん]に残[のこ]ったのは、ただ一本[いっぽん]の松[まつ]のみだった。
examples.en: After the tsunami, all that was left on the shore was a single pine tree.

points.notes: {ただ} here is the adverb 'only, merely', not {ただ} 'free (of charge)' or {ただし} 'however'.

quiz.q: やるべきことは全[すべ]てやった。あとはただ天[てん]に任[まか]せる＿＿だ。
quiz.en: I've done everything I should. All that's left is to leave it to fate.

quiz.q: ＿＿利益[りえき]のみを追求[ついきゅう]する企業[きぎょう]は、長続[ながつづ]きしない。
quiz.en: Companies that pursue nothing but profit don't last long.

points.title: 〜まじき
points.meaning: unbecoming of; that (someone in that position) should never do
points.structure: Noun + に／として + あるまじき + Noun / Verb (dictionary form) + まじき + Noun
points.explanation:
{まじき} is the attributive form of the classical {まじ} 'must not / should not'. It's almost always used in {〜にあるまじき} or {〜としてあるまじき}: 'behaviour that should never exist in someone who is X'. It's a strong moral condemnation of people who betray the standards of their role: teachers, doctors, police, politicians, civil servants.

With other verbs: {許[ゆる]すまじき} 'unforgivable'.

**Register:** formal and written; frequent in news reports and editorials about scandals. It's the negative counterpart of {〜たる者[もの]} (Unit 6).

examples.jp: それは教師[きょうし]にあるまじき行為[こうい]だ。
examples.en: That's conduct unbecoming of a teacher.

examples.jp: 生徒[せいと]に暴力[ぼうりょく]をふるうなど、教育者[きょういくしゃ]にあるまじきことだ。
examples.en: Using violence against students is unforgivable for an educator.

examples.jp: 患者[かんじゃ]の個人[こじん]情報[じょうほう]を漏[も]らすのは、医師[いし]としてあるまじき行為[こうい]だ。
examples.en: Leaking patients' personal information is something a doctor should never do.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもの命[いのち]を奪[うば]うなど、許[ゆる]すまじき犯罪[はんざい]だ。
examples.en: Taking a child's life is an unforgivable crime.

points.notes: Must be followed by a noun ({行為[こうい]}, {発言[はつげん]}, {こと}, {態度[たいど]}).

quiz.q: 客[きゃく]の悪口[わるぐち]をSNSに書[か]き込[こ]むなど、店員[てんいん]＿＿行為[こうい]だ。
quiz.en: Posting insults about customers on social media is behaviour unbecoming of shop staff.

quiz.q: 賄賂[わいろ]を受[う]け取[と]るなど、公務員[こうむいん]としてある＿＿ことだ。
quiz.en: Accepting bribes is something a public servant should never do.

points.title: 〜べからず／〜べからざる
points.meaning: must not (prohibition); indispensable / unforgivable
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + べからず (する → すべからず) / Verb + べからざる + Noun
points.explanation:
{べからず} is the classical negative of {べし} 'should'. It means 'must not' and appears in old-style signs, proverbs and rules — think 'Keep off the grass'.

{べからざる} is its noun-modifying form: {欠[か]くべからざる} 'indispensable (that must not be lacking)', {許[ゆる]すべからざる} 'unforgivable'.

Famous phrases: {初心[しょしん]忘[わす]るべからず} 'never forget your beginner's spirit' (uses classical {忘[わす]る}), {働[はたら]かざる者[もの]食[く]うべからず} 'he who does not work shall not eat'.

**Register:** classical and written. You'll see {べからず} on temple signs, retro notices and in proverbs; {欠[か]くべからざる} in formal writing. Not used in conversation, except jokingly.

examples.jp: 芝生[しばふ]に入[はい]るべからず。
examples.en: Keep off the grass.

examples.jp: 初心[しょしん]忘[わす]るべからず。
examples.en: Never forget the spirit you started with.

examples.jp: 働[はたら]かざる者[もの]、食[く]うべからず。
examples.en: He who does not work, neither shall he eat.

examples.jp: 水[みず]は人間[にんげん]の生活[せいかつ]に欠[か]くべからざるものだ。
examples.en: Water is indispensable to human life.

points.notes: {べからず} ends a sentence; {べからざる} must be followed by a noun. Compare {〜べきではない} 'should not', the modern equivalent.

quiz.q: 「ここにゴミを捨[す]てる＿＿」という看板[かんばん]が立[た]っている。
quiz.en: There's a sign saying 'Do not dump rubbish here'.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は今[いま]やこのチームにとって欠[か]く＿＿存在[そんざい]だ。
quiz.en: He has now become indispensable to this team.

points.title: 〜(よ)うが〜まいが
points.meaning: whether or not; regardless of whether
points.structure: Verb volitional + が + Verb (dictionary form / ない-stem) + まいが / Verb volitional + と + Verb + まいと
points.explanation:
